# Release Notes

This page summarizes user-visible PRFlow changes. For a complete change history, see [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/The01Geek/prflow/releases).

**Release cadence:** PRFlow versions continuously and publishes releases periodically, so a published version number skips the intermediate versions developed between two releases. A gap between consecutive tags is expected and does not mean a release is missing.

**Legacy review tier:** Entries about automatic pull-request-triggered review apply only to repositories that installed that tier before July 29, 2026. Fresh installations do not receive it. Use a collaborator comment with `/prflow:review` for the supported cloud review path.

## October 26, 2026

- **`/prflow:spec` more reliably re-checks the whole draft after audit fixes or a change you ask for, before showing it to you again.** (#3274)

## October 25, 2026

- **`/prflow:spec` can fall back to reading its audit-prompt template directly.** The template now carries the boundary markers the reference load rule requires. (#3178)
- **`/prflow:spec` and `/prflow:implement` refute fewer true `Verified:` quotations that carry `\"`-escaped inner quotes or that a string join or comment splits across source lines.** (#2579)
- **`/prflow:spec`'s audit prompt tells the auditor not to report a finding that rests on search output it never saw.** (#2829)
- **`/prflow:docs-verify --report-file` replies with only the saved report's path.** The two research helpers `/prflow:spec` starts with do the same. (#2941)
- **`/prflow:spec`'s approach question covers each option's recurring cost.** Options can be compared by what each adds to or saves from later runs or uses of the changed system. (#2636)
- **`/prflow:spec` more reliably removes scope and acceptance criteria you never asked for.** Its check now compares the draft with your story, any issue the story names, and your answers to its questions. (#3174)
- **`/prflow:spec`'s re-asked question after research can offer an option in the form the research favors, including one the original menu lacked.** (#2830)
- **Spec asks fewer questions whose options another answer makes wrong or moot.** Fewer questions are re-asked after you pick the approach. (#2882)
- **`/prflow:spec`'s report after each audit round is shorter.** It names each finding briefly, with its grade and whether it was fixed. (#2865)
- **When `/prflow:spec` refines an existing issue, it may reword or merge the issue's acceptance criteria while keeping their requirements.** (#3105)
- **When `/prflow:spec` revises a draft, it now also corrects text in the investigation record (the comment it posts on the issue) that the revision makes false or outdated.** (#3115)
- **`/prflow:spec` checks each term its draft creates or redefines against the files the issue names.** If one of them already uses the term with another meaning, the draft states the change of meaning or uses a different word. (#2723)
- **`/prflow:spec` can end with nothing filed at any implementation-approach question.** Choosing *No change — file nothing* ends the run with no GitHub writes and names any open issue it leaves for you to park, label or close. (#2759)
- **`/prflow:spec`'s early risk research treats a past run's log or record as proof of current behavior only when it confirms which version produced it and what has changed since.** Otherwise it reports the link as not established. (#2550)
- **Implement stops before branch work on an issue that still has its spec `## 🚫 Blocked` section.** The stop names the remedy: settle each open question in the issue, remove the section, then run again. (#3172)
- **Before you pick an approach, `/prflow:spec` can trace a value, text or file the change alters to the code and instructions that read it.** It no longer searches only for the changed name. (#2391)
- **PRFlow's review no longer drops a defect just because the checked text matches an acceptance criterion's wording.** A criterion excuses a defect only when its words cover the whole case. (#2810)
- **`/prflow:implement` no longer adds an "Issue-claim audit: clean" note to the workpad when its check of the issue finds nothing.** (#2914)
- **`/prflow:spec` records each scope answer you give in full: the option's text with its description, or your own words.** The draft's scope is checked against what you chose, not a paraphrase. (#3141)

## October 24, 2026

- **Spec states each motivating case's expected result as what the changed instructions decide for it.** For a change to instructions a model follows, the issue names the deciding instruction, can disqualify a case the changed instructions do not decide as the change requires, and says whether a replayed case needs its original run's context. (#3071)
- **Spec can weigh removing or reusing a repeatedly repaired design element before repairing it again.** (#3145)
- **`/prflow:spec`'s approach question keeps a cost comparison when it shortens one into an option's text.** The short text still says whether the option adds or saves cost compared with current behavior, in which cases, and what remains uncertain. (#3138)
- **Spec audit grading spells out when a false statement or a policy conflict in a draft is a defect.** (#3111)
- **After its second option check, `/prflow:spec` can still remove a proposed part of an option when its reads show every reason for that part false.** The approach question says each removal was not re-checked. (#3099)
- **Spec audits and non-interactive filing require completed draft preparation.** (#3162)
- **`/prflow:review-and-fix` can keep a deferred fix-delta finding deferred when the shadow pass raises it again at the same or a lower severity.** The shadow pass now recognizes that re-raise as the deferral instead of starting an extra iteration. (#2529)
- **Background `/prflow:spec` sessions enter their own worktree before discovery starts.** Discovery and risk agents' report writes are no longer refused partway through, and the run's records stay in one checkout. (#3019)
- **Fix passes compare a prose rule with the other rules deciding its inputs before changing it.** (#3161)
- **`/prflow:spec` can apply an audit suggestion that deletes text or moves it to the investigation record.** The approval question counts each applied one among the corrections. (#3020)
- **`/prflow:spec` re-reads each `Blocked by` prerequisite issue before asking you to file.** It compares the issue's title, body, and open or closed state and close reason with what the design used, and revisits the design before presenting when a change affects it. (#2908)
- **When an issue `/prflow:spec` drafts asks the implementing run to replay or test with a recorded input spec read, such as a retained payload or transcript, it quotes that input's deciding fields.** The quote is JSON-encoded; a long input is quoted near the failure and cited for the rest. (#2317)
- **`/prflow:challenge` judges a change against the user's goal and challenges its linked issue as part of the proposal.** It challenges what the change actually alters first, checks whether anyone relies on behavior the change removes or suppresses, and asks the user when a fact only they hold could change the verdict. (#3218)
- **The `/prflow:spec` investigation record can now post a bulleted, indented or wrapped rejected-candidates line whole.** (#3114)
- **`/prflow:spec` offers to trigger `/prflow:implement` only when `workflows.prflow` is set to `true`.** A list value such as `["true"]` is now treated as unset, so the offer stays off. (#3180)
- **`/prflow:spec` has no clarification question limit.** Replying "just create it" no longer stops the remaining questions. (#3143)

## October 23, 2026

- **`/prflow:spec` checks its own draft the way the auditor will before any audit round.** After fixing a round's findings, it re-checks the whole draft, not only its edits. (#3170)

## October 22, 2026

- **`/prflow:spec` on Claude Code's interactive tier waits for a subagent by ending its turn.** It resumes on that subagent's completion notification instead of busy-polling or redoing the subagent's reads. Headless, nested, Codex and other runs still never end the turn with a subagent pending. (#2847)
- **`/prflow:implement` no longer hand-fixes review-and-fix findings after its review completes.** (#2482)
- **`/prflow:spec` no longer counts a paraphrase or an unchecked conclusion as verified Step 2 evidence.** (#2639)
- **`/prflow:implement` checks acceptance criteria against your issue's Desired Behavior and avoids deleting a check your issue keeps to meet one.** (#2648)
- **`/prflow:spec` asks again about a disproved approach or scope reason as soon as the evidence arrives, and skips needless re-asks.** A sub-choice reply now revises the draft without redrafting it. (#2674)
- **`/prflow:spec` helper agents read GitHub from your own repository.** Helper and audit agents are now told to run GitHub lookups from your checkout instead of naming a guessed repository, and not to read a failed lookup as an empty result. (#3018)
- **Spec issues cite a rule's home instead of copying it.** The spec self-audit can now revise criteria and other issue text to point at the place a rule is already stated. (#2510)
- **Review reports can be assembled by a helper from the rendered checklist pieces.** `normalize-verdicts.py assemble` builds the report from the engine's draft, replacing its token lines with the rendered piece files and placing the issue-compliance file. (#2468)
- **`/prflow:spec`'s research peers no longer repeat each other's whole-repository probes.** Discovery owns the repository-wide searches and measurements, both research reports quote their evidence, and later steps can reuse it instead of reading the same sources again. `/prflow:docs-verify --report-only` reports no longer have a word limit. (#2864)
- **On interactive runs, spec now runs its option check before a follow-up question that chooses a mechanism inside the picked approach.** (#2731)
- **`/prflow:spec` reuses earlier option-check findings later in the run.** Approach questions repeat fewer risks the options already state, and the drafted issue carries related issues and facts the run already found. (#2942)

## October 21, 2026

- **`/prflow:spec` runs an audit round on each saved draft before showing it to you, can offer another audit round with no limit, and shortens the filing question.** The draft path, audit summary line and other notes move out of the question text. (#2982)
- **Issues drafted by `/prflow:spec` state each accepted limit and decision-rule mapping outcome in one place.** Fewer copies can drift apart when the issue is revised. (#2383)
- **Review severity caps no longer promote lower-severity findings.** This prevents a Suggestion from becoming a rejection solely because its cap is Important. (#2399)
- **`/prflow:spec` revisions can ask more questions or record more blocked decisions.** Clarification also searches cited evidence for outcome-deciding terms. (#2989)
- **Cloud workflow templates follow the Claude Code Action v1 release line.** The bundled Claude Code version and model aliases can change between reruns of the same commit. (#2981)
- **Review-and-fix can reuse unchanged checklist verdicts after a promoted iteration.** The review that follows one can carry forward PASSes from the newest earlier iteration that ran Step 1 instead of re-verifying every checklist item. (#2381)
- **`/prflow:implement` can fix and re-review findings left by a capped review loop.** (#2980)
- **The `/prflow:implement` cleanup pass checks rule restatements and coverage claims before review.** The cleanup reviewer reports sentences that misstate a rule and coverage claims a search falsifies. (#3040)
- **Fixes prefer deleting text a review finding flags to rewording it.** `/prflow:review-and-fix` and `/prflow:fix` can spend fewer re-reviews on text a fix rewrote. (#2344)
- **The shared writing standard adds a rule to keep each sentence true at the scope it states.** Writers that load it are told to keep a condition every case shares and to add no limit the source lacks. (#2621)
- **`/prflow:docs-verify --report-file` accepts an absolute path inside the working directory's `.prflow/tmp/`.** `/prflow:spec` discovery no longer passes a path the flag's own rule refuses. (#2918)

## October 20, 2026

- **A plain label bullet such as `- Potential Gotchas` can now end a `- Documentation Needed` list item.** `/prflow:implement` no longer treats the paths under that bullet as required documentation edits, nor reads the deliverables written after it. (#2477)
- **Resumed local `/prflow:implement` runs continue on the open PR's own commits instead of a stale same-named branch.** Branch setup can now stop the run as Blocked rather than continue on a branch it cannot safely update. (#2813)
- **`/prflow:spec`'s option checker sees what discovery found the code actually does.** Its risk investigator can also be given the paths of evidence files saved earlier in the session, such as a downloaded job log. (#2667)
- **Local reviews no longer start building the verification checklist as soon as a checklist generator writes its output file.** (#2551)
- **`/prflow:spec` Step 1 peers can write their own report files, sparing the run its retype of both reports.** `/prflow:docs-verify --report-only` gains a `--report-file` flag that writes its report to a `.prflow/tmp/` path. (#2666)
- **`/prflow:spec` can draft the issue from the risks, corrections and edge cases it recorded earlier in the run, and check the draft against them.** (#2527)
- **A resumed `/prflow:implement` run re-runs the issue-claim audit without first checking for a reusable earlier audit.** `workpad.py` no longer accepts `--record-audit-inputs` or `reuse-check … audit`. (#2451)
- **`/prflow:spec` says in an instruction-change issue whether each motivating case is replayed, and `/prflow:implement`'s pre-review verification skips the replays the issue rules out.** (#2689)
- **`/prflow:challenge` also asks whether another stage, component or owner would solve the problem more cleanly.** (#2915)
- **Implement's progress notes describe version-control steps in plain words.** Local worktree-isolated sessions are less likely to refuse a progress-note write and spend a call sending it again. (#2744)
- **`/prflow:spec` helper agents can lose fewer shell calls on macOS.** The instructions a spec run gives its helper agents now include a rule for searching and reading without the wildcard and `=`-word command shapes zsh rejects. (#2755)
- **`/prflow:spec`'s filing preview lists the choices the run made itself, and its audit-round and risk-investigator briefs no longer present agent-written advice as the user's decisions.** (#2577)
- **`/prflow:spec` can run fewer repeat option checks before each implementation-approach question.** Interactive runs can reach the implementation-approach question sooner and spend fewer subagent tokens. (#2850)
- **`/prflow:implement` replays the old instruction text before any new-text replay of a case the fix exists to change, and skips new-text replays that cannot tell the old text from the new.** Replay actions can be graded from the replay's own tool-call record. (#2638)
- **A case an acceptance criterion accepts can now stop failing checklist verification.** `/prflow:spec` now writes each accepted limit an issue states into an acceptance criterion. (#2682)
- **Review-and-fix can send Suggestion and Minor findings about its own fixes back to the fixer at any threshold.** A defect a fix introduces can be fixed in the same iteration, before the merge review sees it. (#2907)
- **`/prflow:spec` can read to settle a fact the option check left unconfirmed before it asks the approach question.** The question then states what that read found, so a disproved fact can change an option or bring back a passed-over approach before you pick. (#2717)

## October 19, 2026

- **`/prflow:spec` can recommend an approach option that rests on an unconfirmed fact.** The question still shows each such fact as not confirmed. (#2562)
- **On Windows Git Bash, `/prflow:implement`'s issue audit and `/prflow:fix` can read a file as the base branch has it.** They now read it by commit ID, so git no longer answers "Not a valid object name". (#2790)
- **On native Windows, PRFlow's Python helpers now launch the first `bash.exe` in a fully qualified `PATH` folder rather than a bare `bash`, and give a `bash.exe` in a `System32`, `Sysnative` or `WindowsApps` folder absolute paths in WSL's `/mnt/<drive>/…` form.** With no such `bash.exe` they launch `bash`. Set `DEVFLOW_BASH` to choose a bash explicitly. (#2792)
- **On Windows, a review run no longer deletes or moves files through a symbolic link at its shadow review directory.** It acts on the symbolic link itself, not on the folder it points to. A directory junction there is still followed (#2808). (#1193)
- **`/prflow:spec`'s approach question marks facts the run confirmed itself and labels fewer unbacked facts as backed.** Spec can skip an option-check re-run before asking. (#2650)
- **`/prflow:spec`'s option checker can write its own record, and returns the findings that bear on each option for the implementation-approach question to disclose before you pick.** (#2578)
- **The `/prflow:spec` issue template tells drafters to name no other issue in a `Blocked by` reason.** (#2805)
- **The `/prflow:fix` skill defers local test execution to repository policy.** (#2805)
- **`/prflow:spec` collects a subagent's result before continuing, instead of waiting for your next message.** (#2844)
- **`/prflow:spec`'s filing question can show the draft path, the audit summary, the unfixed audit findings and the self-audit summary.** (#2363)
- **Review-and-fix passes re-check fewer settled checklist items.** A passed item on a file a fix edited can now keep its earlier result. (#2353)
- **`/prflow:review-and-fix` and `/prflow:fix` can restate a prose rule as one general clause instead of adding the case a finding says it missed.** (#2523)
- **Reviews fail correct code less often over a checklist claim the review worded itself.** Correct code is less often sent back to be fixed over a requirement only the reworded claim stated. (#2580)
- **Generated pull request titles describe the implemented solution.** (#2848)

## October 18, 2026

- **`/prflow:review-and-fix` can list a shadow review's new low-severity findings in its `## Coverage` report, and can decide "shadow agreed, full coverage" from the findings the loop recorded.** A run no longer picks a route by hand for a shadow that adds only low-severity findings. (#2251)
- **Spec's scope and side questions can name evidence against their recommended answer.** You can see what the run already read that argues against the recommended option before you choose it. (#2513)
- **`/prflow:implement` passes the review-fix worker the digest of its latest prompt-extension check.** A Phase 3 base-update merge that edits the extension no longer stops the run at the worker's digest check. (#2564)
- **Implement runs no longer put their 🎉 or 👎 reaction on an unrelated comment that only mentions the command.** (#2484)
- **`/prflow:spec` can drop a case its own revision added and state the case as a limit, rather than patch it.** A fork question that fixing a finding raises about how to handle a case also offers to leave that case uncovered. (#2541)
- **`/prflow:spec` and `/prflow:docs-verify --report-only` treat cut-short output as an incomplete search.** (#2369)
- **`/prflow:review-and-fix` declines a Suggestion or Minor finding only for a listed reason, and a later fix can re-check an earlier decline.** (#2343)
- **Local reviews can spend less time waiting on checklist verifiers.** A verifier asked to save its verdict is told to finish any check it is still running first. (#2519)
- **`/prflow:spec` can keep your assignment and implementation answers across its approval prompts instead of discarding them.** A later prompt can show a kept answer, and you can change it before you approve. (#2664)
- **`/prflow:spec` walks each motivating case and named rule arm before asking for the design, and `/prflow:implement` keeps replaying the cases an issue names instead of swapping one out.** (#2318)
- **`/prflow:spec`'s failed reference-load fallbacks are shorter and report what they skip.** A run whose reference file fails to load no longer gets compact copies of that file's checks, such as the contract and premise checks, and says which coverage it lost. (#2521)
- **Cloud review, review-and-fix, PR-description and retrospective runs' built-in `gh api` grant now covers only your own repository's endpoints.** The built-in list no longer grants `gh issue create`, `gh issue comment`, `gh pr comment`, `gh pr create`, `env` or `export`; re-run the installer to pick this up, and upgrade `prflow_version` first or together with it. (#2672)

## October 17, 2026

- **`/prflow:review-and-fix <PR>` reviews a branch that carries unpushed local commits instead of stopping.** With `--push-each-iteration`, those earlier local commits are now reviewed with the PR and pushed with the first fix push. (#2068)
- **Local `/prflow:implement` runs without a vendored plugin copy spend fewer tool calls in the intake, review-fix and finalization workers.** Intake and finalization no longer make a separate digest call, the three workers skip the vendored helper path once the run has found it missing, and the documentation and PR-description children are told the vendored folder is absent. (#2454)
- **`/prflow:spec` can ask the implementation-approach question again after you pick, so you choose with the corrected facts instead of approving a patched design.** (#2539)
- **The comment analyzer can grade an unchanged instruction line your change makes false as Critical.** (#2241)

## October 16, 2026

- **Review-and-fix keeps a parked finding parked when the shadow review only adds new evidence.** Before, a re-raise at the same or a lower severity with a different explanation reopened the fix loop just so the finding could be parked again. Now a different explanation alone no longer reopens it, and the new evidence is still recorded with the decision. The gate's other promotion conditions still apply, for example a higher severity, a mis-grade rule match, or a missing or malformed input. (#2335)
- Spec revisions route attacked text before composing a repair, including when an audit supplies no remedy. For example, when the issue template permits removal and that resolves the finding, the brief gets no replacement incidental claim. Needed statements are edited before adding explanation. (#2323)
- Checklist verifiers receive absolute artifact paths for the reviewing checkout, reducing ambiguity when reviews run in worktrees. (#2321)
- **Implement skips a redundant telemetry save after review-and-fix.** When the review-and-fix loop's own exit save already reported `persist-outcome: ok skipped` for this run and nothing relevant changed since, `/prflow:implement` reuses that result instead of running the same save again (about 10 seconds in the recorded case). Missing, failed or uncertain evidence still runs the recovery save. (#2113)
- **The telemetry self-check follows the `telemetry.enabled` master switch.** With the master switch `false`, `lib/efficiency-trace.sh --self-check` now stays silent even when `efficiency_telemetry_enabled` is explicitly `true`, matching `--persist`, which already skips the telemetry branch in that case. (#2113)
- **A run whose iteration records are all malformed now reports `persist-outcome: lost partial-iterations`** instead of `ok skipped`, so the loss is no longer mistaken for telemetry being switched off. (#2113)
- **Review findings cite source-file lines, not patch positions.** `/prflow:review` reviewers now number each finding's lines, and its `defect_signature.line_range`, by their one-based lines in the file they read. A position in the patch never counts as a source line. Content missing or deleted from the current file is described without a current-file line, and its range stays null when no current-file span can be located. A base-file line is marked as base. A location whose file cannot be read, or whose line cannot be found, is marked unverified. The `/prflow:implement` cleanup reviewer also numbers each line one-based from the current working-tree file, never by patch position, and marks a location unverified when its file cannot be read or its line cannot be found. (#2092)
- **`/prflow:review-and-fix` checklists no longer restate earlier iterations' findings.** From the second iteration, the review's checklist builds no item from the earlier findings passed to the review, so no item restating one overrides the reviewers' decision not to raise it again. The reviewers still decide whether such a finding stands, and are told to report again a fix that did not work. (#2374)
- **Report shadow review limits accurately.** Shadow reviews write into a separate directory to reduce accidental discovery of prior findings. Reports no longer claim verified shadow agreement when the engine ran inline in the loop's informed context; separate writes do not isolate reads. (#2244)
- **The review engine no longer retypes resolved acceptance criteria into its return.** When a review resolved one or more criteria, the engine leaves them out of the part it writes and the return assembler (`review-dirty-tree.sh engine-return`) fills `acceptance_criteria` from the resolver's `criteria.json`, so each review entry spends less time on output and later fixes see the resolver's exact text. When that file is absent or unusable, the assembler says so and the engine writes the criteria itself. (#2145, #2481)
- **Keep defects a checklist verifier finds outside its claim.** A verifier that passes a narrow claim can now also report a separate defect it found while checking it. The review lists that defect with the ordinary findings and the fix loop routes it, where before it was lost in the passed item's evidence. (#2240)
- **Review fixes use a focused class search.** The review-and-fix loop no longer loads implementation sweep procedures for each correction, reducing the reference reading needed for small fixes. (#2111)
- **`/prflow:implement`'s review step no longer keeps the `review` extension loaded for its whole run, and a failed review extension load now shows on the workpad.** The review-and-fix worker loads only the `implement` extension. Each review loads the `review` extension itself, including a review that runs inside the loop when its own dispatch fails. The workpad no longer has a `Skill extension resolved: review.md` row, and an older workpad's unticked row of that name no longer blocks Complete or the reuse of a finished review. When a review reports that the `review` extension or a reviewer's extension failed to load, was refused or could not be established, `/prflow:review-and-fix` records it in its reflections, once per extension each time the loop runs, and an implement run also writes it to the workpad; if that write fails, no workpad or pull request records the failed load. A `review` extension that fails to load no longer stops an implement run before its review; the review runs without that policy and reports the failed load. (#1796)
- **`/prflow:implement` can now delete a doc sentence its change makes false, or point it at the rule it describes, when readers do not need it where it is.** (#2337)
- **An implement run no longer runs an extra shadow review just because a review check could not settle an acceptance criterion.** Inside `/prflow:implement`, the review-and-fix loop skips its shadow pass when its first iteration is clean. An inconclusive check on an acceptance criterion, for example one that needs a command run or a CI result, no longer makes that iteration unclean; implement's acceptance-criteria gate, whose verifier can run commands, checks such a criterion later in the run unless it is tagged `(post-merge)`. An inconclusive check on anything else, or any failed check, still rules the skip out. (#2457)
- **`/prflow:spec` checks each design option against what the run recorded before asking you to choose.** Before the implementation-approach question, a separate subagent with a fresh context reads what the run recorded. It checks each option, and each candidate the run dropped, for facts a recorded risk, constraint or edge case qualifies and for facts no checked record confirms. The question then names the ones that bear on each option. An option that rests on an unconfirmed fact is no longer marked `(Recommended)`, unless your repository's prompt extension sets its own recommendation policy; a fact whose kind is unclear is shown but keeps the mark. When the separate check cannot run or returns an incomplete or malformed result, `/prflow:spec` runs the same check itself and the question says the independent check did not run. The self-audit before the draft is shown also checks the draft against the chosen option's listed risks and unconfirmed facts. (#2358)
- **`/prflow:review-and-fix` reads a smaller review result after each review pass.** The review engine's return file now writes each passing checklist row with only its id, verdict, severity, claim signature, verification mode and reuse fields; failing, inconclusive and other rows are written whole. The loop reads that file after every review pass and keeps it in context for the rest of the run, so each iteration costs fewer tokens. The full passing rows stay in the run directory's retained checklist and verification files. (#2474)
- **A review finding that only argues against a decided acceptance criterion no longer rejects a pull request that meets its criteria.** When `prflow_review.verdict_severity_threshold` is `important` or `suggestion`, a finding below Critical whose whole claim is behavior a decided criterion requires, or that asks for what a decided criterion excludes, gives APPROVE with notes instead of REJECT. It stays in the report at its grade, marked `[decided by criterion <N>]`. Some still block, for example a Critical finding, a finding that is partly a real defect, and one whose relation to a criterion is unclear. Inside `/prflow:review-and-fix` the fix loop routes such a finding to the fixer whatever the fix threshold, until its iteration cap. Repositories on the default `critical` threshold see no change. (#1793)
- **`/prflow:spec` no longer shows a FILE verdict that no auditor gave.** The audit summary line no longer carries a FILE or REVISE value, and the approval question now says how many must-revise findings were fixed after the last audit round and whether the final draft was audited. (#2392)
- **Code review no longer passes or fails a checklist item on a line its search did not show.** The checklist verifier reads that line in full before grading on it, and reports the item inconclusive when it cannot. (#2470)
- **`/prflow:spec` posts the investigation record on an existing issue it updates, as it does on a new one.** An updated issue also gets the `PRFlow` label and the assign and implement questions. (#2494)

## October 15, 2026

- **Checklist verification no longer executes shell commands.** Verifiers inspect the supplied source snapshots and PR diff, and report INCONCLUSIVE when a claim needs execution or missing evidence. This removes live shell and API probes from checklist verification. (#2311)
- Clarify spec choices, question dependencies, audit verdicts and publication rules; consolidate existing guidance and keep maintainer evaluation tools out of consumer installs. (#2310)
- **`/prflow:spec`'s fresh-context auditor walks the change instead of scanning for text shapes.** The Step 3.6 audit prompt replaces its eleven-dimension checklist with a five-step walk — readers of removed or changed text, arms of added mechanisms, outcome, premises, criteria — under one bar for every finding: the quoted text, a concrete case, the wrong outcome and the read that shows it. The auditor returns findings only, never replacement wording; a universal claim is a defect only by counterexample; criterion placement, restatement and authoring-shape rules stay with the drafter. Live watches had found about three real defects among fifteen findings per run, most later-round findings attacking text an earlier round's remedy added, and one triage batch's review rejections all deletions or reworded arms nobody had walked. (#2315)
- **`/prflow:spec` researches choices you delegate.** "You decide" or "I don't know" makes it research the question and re-ask it with each option's pros and cons and, where the evidence supports one, a recommendation. A second such reply takes the recommendation, except that it files a new issue rather than widening one and keeps a requested case in scope; with no recommendation, the question goes to Blocked. Each settled choice is named in chat and again before draft approval, or in the final outcome when it ends the run without filing. Delegating a question it recognizes as needing facts only you know sends it to Blocked without research; "just create it" and the question limit still end clarification. (#2301)
- **The review-and-fix fixer changes code for a failed checklist item only when it finds a real defect** — The `/prflow:review-and-fix` fixer reads both the cited source and the requirement behind the claim before editing. Accurate evidence for a requirement the code does not have to meet is pushed back as `claim-quality`, a misread is still pushed back, and a read that settles none of these is pushed back as `uncategorized`, naming what could not be established. (#2259)
- **`/prflow:review-and-fix` can report a fix that did not work.** When the previous iteration's findings reach the review that opens an iteration, that review is told that a finding marked applied records a fix attempt, not a resolved defect, so it can report the finding again while its defect remains. Findings with any other decision are still re-raised only with new evidence. (#2260)
- **Review agents report defects, not fixes** — PRFlow's review agents and the fix-delta reviewer now give each finding's file and line and what is wrong, and suggest no fix, deletion included. The fix loop chooses each fix itself, so it no longer applies a PRFlow reviewer's ready-made fix that adds text and draws the next finding. (#2141)
- **Review checklist items fail less often on inputs that decide nothing.** The checklist verifier now counts a counterexample only when a shipped caller or documented state can produce its input and that input reaches the code or text the claim is about; documented states include, for example, an input anyone outside the repository or a process can send, or a file can carry, through a public interface without a code change. Any other input decides nothing, so the item passes on positive evidence or comes back inconclusive; an input whose producer or reach the verifier cannot settle makes it inconclusive. The generator no longer words a claim around the input in its hint. Reviews raise fewer false FAILs, and the fix loop makes fewer edits to working code. (#2118)
- **Spec pairs current-state discovery with independent early risk investigation.** The second parallel peer now checks request-specific assumptions and conditional failure paths before clarification and approach selection. Discovery keeps its complete coverage contract, failures retain usable evidence with explicit gaps, and the later draft audit remains unchanged. (#1832)
- **Discovery and planning follow your selected model.** Code Explorer and Code Architect use the implementation run's model by default. You get this through the normal plugin update. (#2380)
- **Faster `/prflow:review-and-fix` iterations.** The reviewer that checks each fix now loads your `review-and-fix` extension itself, so the loop no longer copies the whole extension into every check. That saves about 30 seconds per check for a 9–10 KB extension. The reviewer applies the extension only when it loads a copy matching the one the loop loaded; otherwise it reports the check as not verified. If your vendored PRFlow is too old to report the extension's fingerprint, these checks run without your extension, and the loop says so in its reflections until you upgrade. Review loops without a live progress comment, such as those `/prflow:implement` runs, also stop saving review-agent output files that nothing reads, so verification starts sooner. Standalone reviews and their PR comments are unchanged. (#2119)
- **Local review retry rounds no longer idle on a verifier that already replied.** On the local tier, the wait after a `/prflow:review` refused-launch retry round now expects only the verifiers that round started and earlier ones that have not handed back. A verifier that handed back without writing its verdict goes straight to delivery recovery, saving about 60 seconds per affected retry round. (#2269)
- `/prflow:implement` Phase 2 skips the code explorer when the orchestrator's own reads of the requirements, audit findings, documentation map and current source establish that no question about existing behavior or affected consumers remains; otherwise it dispatches the explorer for the remaining questions. A dispatched explorer answers just those questions with findings that change the plan or expose consequential uncertainty, states it found none, or reports what it could not complete (#2014).
- **Local implement and review-and-fix runs stop spending calls that always fail.** PRFlow's subagents now carry the cloud's refused command shapes in their own instructions instead of reading `.prflow/tmp/command-shapes.md`; only the review engine still reads that file, in the same message as its first other Read. After one decisive miss on the vendored extension loader or review skill, a subagent skips `.prflow/vendor/prflow/` for the rest of its run. `/prflow:implement` skips its vendored-version check once its start-up probe has found no vendored folder, and the review engine looks up both vendored engine locations in one step. Cloud runs keep the vendored path first. (#2147)
- **Spec reduces unnecessary preservation criteria.** For example, when your request is readable, a file's presence in the planned changes no longer justifies freezing it, and guarantees already required by project guidance stay with review. Requested restrictions keep their scope and form. If you need something kept as it is, say so in your request. (#2116)

## October 14, 2026

- **Removed the review-skills refactor's unused helper surfaces, effort-telemetry fields and workflow step.** `checklist finalize … --no-groups` now exits 2 with the helper's usage error, `resolve-review-overrides.py --effort-json` is refused by its argument parser, and the `view-materialize` subcommand is gone from both `review-dirty-tree.sh` (exits 2, unknown subcommand) and `review-engine-io.py`; engine setup still builds the source views, and the producer's stderr summary line now starts `source-view:` with the same fields. The fix loop's iteration record drops `dispatched_effort`, so `install-record` refuses a draft that still holds it, and the telemetry record drops its per-iteration `agent_effort` block and `dispatched_effort_present` flag while staying at `schema_version` 1. The cloud workflows lose the inert `Export provider effort capability to job env` step that wrote `PRFLOW_EFFORT_SUPPORTED`; `--effort` is still gated on the provider step's `effort_supported` output. The config backfill no longer carries its never-firing Haiku effort guard; the cleanup pass still removes `effort` from a Haiku-pinned `agent_overrides` entry. Mixed versions get no compatibility path: older skill text calling a removed surface, or writing `dispatched_effort`, fails against a newer helper copy. (#1884)
- **`/prflow:spec`'s Step 3.5 self-audit reports less.** Its summary now lists what it
  found, what it revised for each finding, and anything it left unfinished or unverified. It no
  longer asks for a line per check that found nothing. The checks themselves still run. A spec
  prompt extension that cites the removed per-check lines or counts should stop citing them. (#2090)
- **`/prflow:spec` now runs a pre-mortem on its design for the whole run.** From the first
  candidate approach until the run ends, it asks what the fix could break, checks each failure
  mode against the code, and drops the ones the change cannot cause. The approach question now
  lists each option's failure modes beside its limits and cost, so you can choose around a
  gotcha before the issue is drafted. (#2262)
- **`/prflow:spec` asks for fewer evidence states when the evidence is prose a model reads.** When
  a draft lets evidence excuse a case from a rule, or loosen, skip or demote its outcome, and that
  evidence is prose a model reads (a line in another agent's reply, for example), the draft now
  covers the cases the issue template already routes for a value an agent reads: absent, its
  producing step failed, or unresolvable. Before, it had to cover four states: missing, malformed
  or wrong-type, produced by a step that did not run, and unreadable. Each case still keeps its
  previous outcome unless the request names it, and a new rule still states each one's outcome.
  Evidence a program parses, such as a file or a field, still covers all four. (#2237)
- **`/prflow:spec` lists each clause of the text an issue changes.** When a drafted issue
  deletes, replaces, moves, rewrites or exempts a case from text with more than one clause, arm
  or ordered step, whatever the draft calls that text, the investigation record lists each clause,
  arm and step by its quoted opening words as kept, moved to a named place, or removed, and the
  acceptance criteria name each one that is moved or removed. The Step 3.5 self-audit checks the issue
  body against this rule. Before, the rule applied only when a criterion's subject was a rule, so
  it missed text a draft called reporting. (#2238)
- **`/prflow:fix` stops unless you are on the pull request's branch.** For a bound pull request,
  the pass now stops, changing nothing, unless the current branch is the pull request's
  `headRefName` or tracks it (`refs/heads/<headRefName>` or `refs/pull/<n>/head`); a detached
  `HEAD` stops too. Before, a branch stacked on the pull request passed and received the fixes.
  The branch update now merges only the base branch for a pull request, and the final branch-sync
  report measures the head against a fresh `headRefOid` read instead of a remote branch fetched
  by name, which on a fork pull request was absent or the wrong branch. (#2219)
- **`/prflow:spec` revisions no longer print a revision-delta census.** The revision check still verifies the facts each edit introduces, keeps a refuted or unverified fact out of the draft, and checks and corrects draft consistency; it no longer requires the per-class walk, falsifiable-zero entries, locator log or the closing `revision-delta check:` line. (#2091)
- `review` no longer runs `pr-test-analyzer` on a diff whose changed files all have config-only extensions (`.md`, `.json`, `.yml`, `.yaml`, `.toml`, `.ini`, `.lock`, `.txt`) just because a path contains `test` or `spec`, such as a Markdown-only edit under `skills/spec/`. A `test`/`spec` path in any other file still marks the diff as test-relevant. (#2120)
- **`/prflow:implement`'s relocation sweep runs its cross-line search without the Grep tool.**
  When the session has no Grep tool, the sweep now runs its cross-line phrase search with
  `rg -U --hidden` instead of recording that search unrunnable; it is unrunnable only when
  neither form can run. (#2256)
- **Review agents search the whole source view.** The six `/prflow:review` reviewers and the
  checklist verifier now search a review's source view including hidden paths such as `.github/`,
  `.prflow/` and `.changeset/` and files an ignore rule matches. Before, the search forms these
  agents used could skip those files, so a reference a change left behind in one of them could pass
  review. Searches of the working tree are unchanged. (#2242)
- **`/prflow:spec` Testing Strategy records gathered evidence, not what the implementing run can verify.** The issue template now asks a draft to record the evidence already gathered and its limits, leaving to the implementing run whether to gather more, instead of disclosing evidence unavailable on the target environment and a resulting readiness limit. (#2268)
- **In-run reviewers no longer report Documentation Needed pages and Testing Strategy results as missing.** Under `/prflow:implement`, the review brief now states that the run writes the issue's Documentation Needed pages after review and records Testing Strategy check results on the issue workpad, so neither is a finding when absent from the diff or PR description; an existing line the diff makes false, and a test the Testing Strategy asks the change to add, are still findings. Standalone `/prflow:review` and `/prflow:review-and-fix` briefs are unchanged. (#2234)
- `/prflow:spec`: the contracts quality group's universal-quantifier row and its degraded copy now accept, as scoped with no rewrite, a universal claim about current code that a read confirms (each text states its exact conditions) (#2231).
- `/prflow:pr-description` now finds the current branch's pull request and updates its body in place, including the deferred review findings it previously missed. When it cannot tell whether the branch has a pull request, it reports why and leaves the pull request body unchanged. A comment-triggered cloud run still starts on the default branch and does not update the body (#2243).
- **A wrong checklist claim over correct code is settled in one answer.** The review's checklist verifier now reports one of four verdicts: PASS, FAIL, INVALID or INCONCLUSIVE. INVALID means your code is right and only the checklist's own generated claim is wrong; on an item whose claim the checklist wrote, other than an acceptance-criterion check or a re-check of an earlier finding, the review records a wording-only pass at once, instead of sending the item to a second verifier whose answer could turn a non-issue into a rejection. Reports no longer carry a "Checklist errors" line: no failed checklist item is set aside from the verdict any more. Scripts that call the bundled `normalize-verdicts.py` helper's `prepare`, `collect`, `render` or `reverify-add` directly must now pass `--contract 2`. (#2138)
- **`preflight.py lint-changed --fail-on-findings` prints where each failing linter's output is.**
  Directly after the `LINT-CHANGED findings ops=<ids>` line, it prints one
  `LINT-CHANGED op=<op id> receipt=<path>` line per id, in the same order. `<path>` is the
  absolute path of the receipt this run wrote for that op, with forward slashes on Windows; when the
  linter ran, the receipt's `findings` field holds its output, so a caller no longer searches the receipt
  directory. A receipt path containing a line break is not printed, and the run exits 2. Other
  output and exit codes are unchanged. (#2140)
- **`/prflow:implement` checks a criterion about prose by reading the prose.** At the final
  acceptance-criteria check, a criterion about what a skill, agent instruction, document or
  comment says is now tagged `source-read`. Its verifier passes it on a read of that text at the
  run's head, with a pointer to the lines read and how they cover the criterion. It no longer
  needs an unrelated lint or test run that proves nothing about the text. A criterion about a
  refusal or rejection, a program's output or exit status, or a measured value still needs an
  executed command, as do test, lint and build criteria. When the verifier reports that a
  `source-read` or `non-command` criterion needs a stricter kind of check, the run re-checks it
  under the next stricter class (`non-command`, then `command`) instead of routing it to the fix,
  rewrite, defer or Blocked steps. Only a run whose start-up check finds the vendored copy at the
  plugin's version, or finds no vendored copy, uses the new class; on any other outcome those
  prose criteria stay `non-command`, as before. (#2246)
- **`/prflow:implement` runs its cleanup pass in Phase 2, before the sweeps and tests, and deletes, merges or rewords text only when every outcome of it that an acceptance criterion, a scope decision, a plan step serving one or a remaining rule still needs survives the edit.** Phase 2's sweeps, tests, motivating-case replays and commits now cover the cleanup's edits; there is no separate `refactor:` cleanup commit and no cleanup step after the draft pull request opens. A finding PRFlow cannot confirm stays unapplied, is recorded on the workpad and never blocks the run. (#2236)
- **Review agents filter searches by file type without a glob.** The `/prflow:review`
  reviewers narrow a search by file type only with `rg -t <type>` (for
  example `-t md`). Before, zsh could refuse an unquoted
  `--include=*.md` before the search ran, and a shell could expand an unquoted `-g *.md` into the
  wrong files, so local runs wasted calls. (#2142)
- **`/prflow:spec` asks when a word in your request means something different in your repository.** Before its first clarification questions, `/prflow:spec` now compares the words in your request that name a thing, its owner, a state, a scope or a relationship with what those words mean in the evidence it already gathered and in `glossary.md` at your internal-docs root. When a word means something else in your repository, or could name more than one thing there, and the difference changes, or may change, what gets built, it asks you which meaning you intend before writing the acceptance criteria, unless your request already states its meaning and names the repository meaning it replaces. Words that match cost no extra question, and a non-interactive run lists these questions under the issue's Blocked section. (#2302)
- `/prflow:review` can now treat a finding already rejected on the pull request as settled (#2299). `/prflow:fix`, and the `/prflow:review-and-fix` fixer on a numbered pull request run with `--push-each-iteration`, can record an evidence-backed rejection as a `Finding rejected "<finding>": <evidence>` line in the PR description, and `/prflow:pr-description` keeps those lines. When the PR author is the GitHub Actions bot or trusted under `allowed_bots`/`allowed_users`, later reviews of the pull request read the lines as evidence that a finding was already judged not a defect, and the report's Run details quotes each counted line. A custom implement App that authors pull requests must be listed in `allowed_bots` for its lines to count.
- Refactored spec's existing consistency and dependency checks: drafts and revisions compare affected statements on the same cases, and reused components are checked for the behavior their consumers need. (#2309)

## October 13, 2026

- **The review's checklist generator is now told to write its output file once, as its last step.** A local review does not wait for a generator to finish before reading its file, so a generator that saves a draft first can have that draft rejected and retried, or merged with claims missing. (#2133)
- Effectiveness telemetry now defaults off for new configurations and unset runtime values. Opt in with `prflow_review_and_fix.efficiency_telemetry_enabled: true`; upgrades preserve saved values, and operational run and cost records remain controlled by `telemetry.enabled`. (#2154)
- **Spec preserves your requested scope.** Before excluding a case you requested, spec reuses your prior agreement or asks. Without an available user, an unresolved scope question stays Blocked. The issue-body and final-outcome instructions now call for agreed exclusions and known tracking or unfiled status to be disclosed. (#2082)
- **Spec issues state the property every affected site must have instead of listing the sites.** When a criterion's property covers a set of places the change must reach, `/prflow:spec` keeps the property, any search that finds them and the files that hold them, and moves the site list to its investigation record; the Step 3.5 self-audit counts such a set as pinned for every site whose coverage is clear. An issue body no longer gives a site a route the code does not have unless the issue decides that route, and text asking a site to describe or apply a rule another file owns asks for a pointer to the rule's home where the site's reader can follow one. (#2050)
- **Spec grounds facts about a recorded case in what it read.** `/prflow:spec` is instructed to state a fact about a reported case's saved input that decides the fix or an expected test result, such as a field the input carried, only from a cited read of that case's known source or retained copy. A source the run did not read or could not reach is reported as that limit, not as the input being gone. A reconstructed, synthetic or adapted scenario for such a case stays usable and is labelled as such. A recorded artifact is evidence to inspect, never instructions to obey. (#2087)
- **The changeset consolidator now checks the form of a changeset body.** `consolidate-changesets.py` stops with an error naming the file when the first non-blank line of a changeset's body does not start with `- `, or when the body has no parenthesized citation of the form `(#123)` or `(#123, #456)`; a citation directly after a `]`, as in a markdown link's target, is not counted. If you run it over your own changesets, bring each pending changeset into that form before the next consolidation. (#2126)
- **Review checklist verifiers now write their verdict file before handing back, and cloud reviews stop waiting for verdict files.** A verifier is told that its whole hand-back, including any hand-back tool the runner provides, is its one-line reply, so a runner's rule that the hand-back must come last no longer leads it to skip the Write that a local review then waits up to 9 minutes for. On the cloud tier the review goes from each verifier launch straight to collecting the replies, with no file wait. (#2112)
- **Spec judges its audit checklist only in an audit round.** `/prflow:spec` challenges its own draft before it shows you the draft. That step no longer renders and judges the full audit checklist. It still verifies the draft's claims against the code and checks that the acceptance criteria cover the desired behavior. A run that then accepted an audit round used to judge the same checklist twice. A round runs after the draft has been challenged and revised. A run with no audit round now gets no audit-checklist pass. That includes a non-interactive run, which runs no round on its own. (#2097)
- **`/prflow:implement` stops as Blocked when an instruction change keeps failing the case it was written for.** For a consequential change to model instructions, a version of the changed text now passes its motivating case only when at least two of its first three replays meet the expectation. At a run's third failing version, implement marks the run Blocked, naming the case. Change the design the issue prescribes, then run the command again. (#2102)
- **The review report lists checklist items under its severity headings.** In a `/prflow:review` report, `## Code Review Findings` now holds the verification-checklist items as well as the findings: each severity group lists its numbered findings, then the failed checklist items of that grade, and inconclusive items sit under `### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred`. The separate `## Verification Checklist Results` section is gone: the checklist tally and the passing items move into the collapsed `## Run details` block, and a `Coverage shortfall:` line now sits in `## Verdict`, after the `Rule applied:` line. A checklist item's group follows its grade, not whether it blocks; the verdict line still says what blocks. The inert-prose cap is now judged for every failed checklist item graded critical or important, at every `verdict_severity_threshold` value, and a capped item is grouped under its capped grade; its line still names the severity it was stored with. With the threshold set to `suggestion`, a critical checklist failure the cap covers no longer counts as Critical in the verdict `/prflow:review-and-fix` gives when its shadow pass still has unresolved findings at the iteration cap, as was already the case at the other thresholds. (#2190)
- `/prflow:implement` Phase 3.4 now passes the evidence verifier the path of the validated Phase 3.3 review-fix handoff when that handoff lists unresolved findings, and the verifier checks each `unresolved_findings` entry against the criteria as a candidate counterexample: one describing a case inside a criterion's stated terms makes it `unmet` when reproduced, or `unestablished` when it cannot be settled; a refuted entry, or one describing no case inside any criterion's terms (a criterion-conflict dispute included), changes nothing. A handoff that was passed but cannot be read or lacks that array leaves every criterion `unestablished`. A criterion such an entry made `unmet` takes the gate's `fix:` commit and re-verification like any other; the gate does not review that fix. `/prflow:review-and-fix`'s rule that a caller fixing the findings left unresolved at the iteration cap re-establishes independent coverage over the fix now allows a fix the caller's own instructions except. (#2125)
- **Merged review checklist items quote the place they point to.** When a review writes its checklist in several batches, each merged item now comes from one claim, keeping a claim that quotes the source when the group has one, so the quote, file and line always match. An item whose provenance value is a list or an object no longer stops the checklist step. (#2203)
- **A false comment about an input no code sends can now be capped as wording.** When a checklist item fails at `important` because a comment or docstring overstates what uncalled code handles, the behavior-inert prose rule can now cap it if, among other conditions, a caller search finds no caller. It can still reject, for example at the `important` threshold when a tool or agent reads that comment or it reaches readers outside the repository, or at the `suggestion` threshold. A capped item's evidence names the caller search and its result. (#2218)

## October 12, 2026

- **`lib/efficiency-trace.sh --correct-iter` is removed; a caller now gets exit 2.** The manual repair of a malformed iteration record already saved on the telemetry branch had no caller in PRFlow. `--correct-iter` and its four operands, `--run-id`, `--iter`, `--corrected-file` and `--expected-digest`, are now refused as an unknown argument with exit 2, under any action. Called without those operands, `--persist` and `--self-check` work as before, except that the `--persist` warning for a run whose effectiveness record omits a malformed iteration no longer names a repair command; that run still reports `lost partial-iterations`, and its record can no longer be repaired in place. (#2152)
- **Recover missing verifier files before repeating a review.** Reviews request a missing answer file once from its original verifier and preserve existing findings when delivery fails. Missing evidence remains unverified. You get this through the normal plugin update. (#2136)
- **Serious fix-delta review findings, pushed-back ones included, no longer take the clean-iteration shortcut.** The clean fast path is kept, and gate pushbacks are reported even when another gate outcome takes precedence. A later fix or disposition in the same iteration supersedes the earlier deferral; calibration and other bookkeeping retain it. Historical review evidence is preserved.
- **`lib/efficiency-trace.sh --mode record` is removed; a caller now gets exit 2.** The mode printed the per-run effectiveness record to standard output and had no caller in PRFlow. `--mode`, with any value or none, is now refused as an unknown argument with exit 2, under any action. A call with neither `--persist` nor `--self-check` prints a usage message naming both on standard error and exits 2. `--persist` still derives the same record and writes it to the telemetry branch, and `--self-check` is unchanged. The mixed-`source` warning, which only record mode printed, is gone. (#2153)
- **A review no longer rejects a pull request over a guarantee nobody wrote.** The review's checklist now drops an absolute claim ("never", "every", "cannot") that does not quote the change's own text, so it is never checked or graded. Other checklist items are checked and graded as before. (#2084)
- **A failed checklist item the fix loop declined no longer keeps rejecting later iterations.** From its second pass on, `/prflow:review-and-fix` used to carry the previous pass's failed checklist items into the next one and check them again, so a failure the loop had declined to fix failed again and held the verdict at REJECT. Now only a passed item can carry over, keeping its earlier result when, among other conditions, its cited files are unchanged. A defect that remains is left to the checklist built fresh at each pass, the fix-delta check and any later `/prflow:review`. (#2148)
- **`/prflow:spec` audit rounds no longer pay for bookkeeping.** An audit round now costs one auditor dispatch and your reading of its findings. The audit state tool and the staged draft write are gone: the run keeps one working-draft file, which it edits, presents, audits and posts as the issue body, with the title in a file beside it. The audit summary line is shorter. It shows rounds run, the must-revise, advisory and invalid counts, the unresolved must-revise count, and whether the draft is byte-for-byte the one the latest verdict round audited. One *Create* option replaces *Create it as-is* and *File anyway*. After filing from the saved draft file, PRFlow reads the issue body back and reports whether it matches the draft. (#2077)
- **Review-and-fix stops paying an extra round for fixes that cannot change a REJECT.** When an iteration that ends in REJECT otherwise converges, the loop now runs another iteration only when that iteration fixed one of the items driving the REJECT, or when it fixed something and the REJECT drivers or fix records cannot be confirmed. A fix to any other finding, whatever its severity, no longer forces that extra review by itself; when the fix-delta check runs, it still reviews them. (#2151)
- **`/prflow:spec` fresh-context audit rounds are now told which issue the run amends and the choices you made.** The fresh-context auditor receives the number of the issue the draft replaces, when the run amends one, and the decisions you made during the run, and is instructed not to report that issue as the draft's duplicate and to name the decision, and the defect that justifies reopening it, in any finding that argues against one of your choices. Each audit round also no longer generates a separate instructions file first, and its return file is always under `.prflow/`, even in a checkout that still has only a `.devflow/` directory. (#2105)
- **`/prflow:spec` no longer pushes approach recommendations toward stronger enforcement by default.** Step 2 used to require a deterministic candidate whenever you proposed a wording change, to name the strongest mechanism it could find, and to step its recommendation up whenever the problem did not say a failure was tolerable. It now considers the relevant alternatives and recommends the least costly approach the checked evidence supports, explaining that approach's limits and maintenance cost; an unclear requirement is asked about rather than answered with a heavier mechanism. (#2089)
- **Verification now matches the change's risk and existing coverage.** Implementation and fix runs can reuse sufficient coverage or direct checks instead of always adding tests first. Reviewers focus on consequential gaps, while your repository's testing requirements and agreed criteria remain binding. Reproducing bugs with a failing test stays preferred, and reported results distinguish completed checks from unavailable evidence. (#2187)
- **Safer proportionate verification.** Unresolved checks require sufficient evidence before a fix is reported resolved. Mutation-backup recovery preserves later edits, and coverage reviews distinguish consequential gaps from optional improvements. (#2195)
- **Review-and-fix records less bookkeeping and reports accurate applied-fix counts.** Opt-in effectiveness telemetry now counts applied decisions, reports unknown input as unestablished, and no longer labels fix-applying iterations as adding nothing. (#2122)
- **Review agents assess the prepared diff and read each acceptance criterion once.** Review agents now review the diff the review prepared, instead of building their own comparison against a newer base. If that diff cannot be opened, they report that they returned no results. A review brief no longer repeats the issue's Acceptance Criteria section when it matches the criteria the brief already lists. (#2134)
- **`/prflow:spec` drafts no longer write out what the change leaves alone.** The drafter still makes the same reads. A criterion can now point at the file that owns a set instead of listing it. An unchanged row quotes the old rule only where that rule contradicts itself, and a removed outcome whose loss is stated as accepted needs no fixture. A verified premise quotes only the clause that makes it true, without listing the other clauses read. (#2104)
- **The Documentation Needed gate now recognizes plain colon, period, and label-only openers.** A handwritten issue body whose deliverable bullet read `- Documentation Needed:` — or with a period, a bare label, or a period/em dash inside the bold label — extracted no deliverable paths, so the Phase 4.1 documentation cross-check silently skipped. Plain and inside-bold labels now accept one common separator set (none, em dash, colon, or period), with the no-separator plain form required to end the line so extended labels stay closed, and the Stage 1 safety-net note recognizes the same spellings. (#2131)
- **Reviews spend less on checklist items that something else already checks.** When the review's checklist generator is sure a claim only restates an acceptance criterion (which the review already verifies as its own item), or that a test, lint or CI check the generator can name already asserts the claim against the real code, it leaves the claim out; when unsure, it keeps the claim. Matching repo-wide convention claims from new review batches, such as license headers, share a checklist item that names their cited files. Each claim is worded so the input its hint names would disprove it. (#2094)

## October 11, 2026

- **A re-checked finding whose recorded behavior is still there but harms nothing now passes.** When a pull request review re-checks an item from the previous review and the code still shows the behavior the earlier finding recorded, the item passes with evidence opening `No defect:` when nothing that reads that behavior fails because of it, it causes none of the harms the review grades severity by, such as wrong output, lost data or a security gap, any cost it adds is bounded by its inputs, and no decided criterion requires otherwise. That reason never applies, and the evidence says why, in cases including when the review cannot show that, when the decided criteria are missing or unusable, or when the earlier finding shows a statement still untrue in the reviewed code, or reports a missing test of changed code or a broken explicit project rule. Such a pass moves no finding of the same review to `Informational — Deferred`. (#2067)
- **`/prflow:spec` checks the text a finding attacks before revising the draft.** At each revision — the Step 3.5 self-audit, an audit round, and a change you request at Step 4 — the run now loads the revision rule before editing, and reports when it cannot. For a finding, attacked text the brief does not need is deleted or moved to the investigation record, and an auditor's suggested fix is weighed as one option rather than pasted in. The audit prompt likewise asks for a finding against a stated heuristic never to be fixed by adding the case: when deleting the attacked text is not enough, the fix restates the heuristic. (#2078)
- **The review-and-fix loop now checks draft iteration records against a shared schema to catch misplaced pushbacks.** The new `loop-verdict-marker.py install-record` step refuses a misplaced `pushbacks` array with a pointer to `fix_decisions`. If neither installer form prints JSON or two corrections are refused, the loop logs the write failure and saves directly; that fallback can leave an unchecked record on disk. Readers warn about unknown top-level keys, and a resumed run no longer restores a synthesized or standalone-review record. (#2038)

## October 10, 2026

- **`/prflow:spec` reads its degradation-routing table only when a reference load fails.** A step whose condition calls for a fallback file now names that file and loads it directly, so condition-triggered fallbacks no longer read the table first. The table drops its row for itself (the skill root's own paragraph covers a failed load of the table) and its marker-contract column. (#1829)

## October 9, 2026

- **A cloud `/prflow:review` longer than one hour now posts its verdict.** With a reviewer App configured (`DEVFLOW_REVIEWER_APP_ID`), the `devflow.yml` command job now runs the long-run credential refresher on `/prflow:review` too. It uses the new `refresh-app-credentials.sh loop-token-file` mode, which mints from the reviewer App at exactly the reviewer mint's permission set, now declared once as `DEVFLOW_REVIEWER_PERMISSIONS`. It refreshes only the `gh` token file and leaves the review checkout's `GITHUB_TOKEN` credential untouched. When the vendored refresher predates that mode, the review path launches nothing and logs one warning. The refresher now passes the App JWT to `curl` on stdin rather than in its argument list, on every path. (#1980)
- **`/prflow:spec` offers a further audit round on one rule, under one cap of three rounds.** At the approval question, the audit-round option is now withheld whenever, among other cases, the current draft already carries a clean audit verdict, the latest round's must-revise findings are waiting on a revision or uncounted, or the run has funded three rounds. Every `REVISE` round now takes the revise cycle, reversing #1918's note that a final-byte pass's `REVISE` findings go to your election: the separate final-byte pass, its extra round slot, and the coverage and calibration offer grounds are gone, so a run opens at most three audit rounds in total. A clean round with thin coverage or an unevidenced advisory finding is no longer re-offered. Runs that elect no audit round load a shorter Step 4 reference. (#1860)
- **A re-checked finding that a decided acceptance criterion settles now passes, with no `Disputed criterion` line.** When a pull request review can read the issue's decided criteria, it gives them to every item it re-checks from the previous review, whatever the description holds. Such an item passes when a criterion's words require the behavior the earlier evidence called a defect, or exclude what the earlier finding asks, and the code shows that behavior. A finding that repeats only that earlier finding moves under `Informational — Deferred` with a `[settled by criterion <N> — confirmed by <item id>]` annotation, and the review re-checks such an item's failure at or above the severity threshold once when a criterion settles its point. The fix skills still write `Disputed criterion` lines as a prompt to amend the issue or accept the criterion, but no review rule acts on them and `Run details` no longer reports them. (#1671)
- **The review-and-fix loop repairs a mistyped engine-return field in one helper call instead of running the whole engine inline, and files no follow-up issue for a deferral a later iteration decided.** `review-dirty-tree.sh engine-return` now also refuses these shapes `entry-close` grades `malformed`: a `diff_profile` or `cap_drops` that is not an object, a present `phase4_demoted` or `reject_drivers` that is not an array of strings (`null` included), and a non-string reviewer-roster element (a shadow entry's failed agents excepted). The engine fixes the named field and re-assembles; both helpers share one shape check. When `loop-verdict-marker.py build-deferrals` exits 1 on an unusable final iteration record or a failed manifest write, it now removes an earlier `deferrals.json` (naming one it cannot remove in its error `reason`), so `/prflow:implement` no longer files that superseded manifest's deferrals. (#2002)
- **`/prflow:fix` and the review-and-fix loop check every fix against the acceptance criteria, wording-only edits included.** A clarification that contradicts a criterion — for example one that edits text a criterion keeps unchanged — is now declined through the existing criterion-conflict path instead of committed, and findings the fix-delta gate sends back for repair get the same check. (#2027)
- **`/prflow:spec` no longer retries a failed config read before offering implementation.** When `/prflow:spec` cannot read whether the cloud implement tier is enabled, it now withholds the "post `/prflow:implement`" offer straight away and says the tier state could not be established. It no longer falls back to reading the config file another way, so the separate *config unreadable* reason is gone. You can still file and assign the issue as before. (#1830)
- **`/prflow:review-and-fix` passes its PR number to each review pass.** A pull-request review pass no longer fails setup with `--mode head-override needs a numeric --pr` and then looks the PR up again; a current-branch run passes no PR and keeps current-branch setup. (#2013)
- **A fanned-out review engine hands its report back as a Markdown file instead of a hand-escaped JSON string.** The engine writes the Phase 4.1 report to its run directory's `verdict-body.md` and passes it to `review-dirty-tree.sh engine-return --report-file`, which reads it as UTF-8 into the return's `report` field without removing the source. `entry-open` deletes any leftover `verdict-body.md` when the next engine entry starts, so a later entry never reuses an earlier entry's report. A missing, unreadable, non-UTF-8, empty or whitespace-only file, an input aliasing the return JSON or its `.tmp` staging file, or an authored `report` supplied alongside it, is refused with a named error. The return file's schema is unchanged, and a call without `--report-file` still takes `report` from the authored JSON. (#2024)
- **`/prflow:implement` now finishes a run whose review you explicitly waived, instead of stopping again at completion.** When you tell a run to skip review and continue, finalization carries that instruction and its source through to the `Complete` write. The waiver skips only the review-coverage check, writes no review record, and adds a workpad note saying review was waived and the change is unverified by review. Every other completion check still applies, and a run with no such instruction from you still needs its review-coverage record. (#2026)
- **`/prflow:review` keeps a verifier's completed answer when only its verdict file is missing, instead of verifying the item again and re-running the whole review.** When a checklist verifier returns a valid verdict but does not write its attempt file, the engine sends that same verifier one `SendMessage` asking it to write the answer it already returned to the same file. The verifier-written file is still required evidence, and the item is not verified again. A delivered file whose verdict, severity or other grading fields differ from the reply is stored INCONCLUSIVE. When the verifier cannot be reached, or the file is still absent afterwards, the item keeps its answer but the evidence check names it `delivery-failed:<id>`: the review-and-fix loop does not re-run the review for it, sends a REJECT's other findings to the fix pass, and otherwise reports the failure. Any other missing verdict file keeps its one re-run. The review engine and review-fix worker agents and the generated cloud workflow allowlists now grant `SendMessage`; a copied workflow without that grant reports the delivery as a failure. (#2022)
- **The review troubleshooting page now states what a failed verdict post needs.** Both the failed job and the review stall backstop's renewed review request need the installed workflow and the vendored PRFlow helpers to be current. (#1979)
- **The review-and-fix loop now handles renames whose new path was added with `git add -N`.** `entry-close` and the per-dispatch dirty-tree check read the work-tree rename as one record pair, so a short original path no longer reads as malformed. A rename present at `entry-open` is preserved; for one the engine creates during the window on the status-snapshot route, `entry-close` restores the original from HEAD and unstages the new file while keeping it on disk. `entry-close` also names a failing `git hash-object` on its before snapshot, or git failing to start, instead of reporting a mismatched or unreadable snapshot. (#1983)
- **A test's own RED-to-GREEN run now discharges the mutation check.** `/prflow:implement`, `/prflow:fix` and `/prflow:review-and-fix` no longer repeat a mutation check that a test's own RED-to-GREEN run already proved: a RED at the same assertion, for the same defect, with nothing bearing on that failure changed since but the fix it drove, discharges it. A mutation still runs for anything that RED did not demonstrate, such as a preserved behavior the unfixed code already satisfied.
- **Under `/prflow:implement`, the review-and-fix loop no longer runs `gh pr checkout` when it enters review.** Implement's checkout already holds the PR branch, so Step 0.5 goes straight to the `branch-sync` gate, which still stops on a mismatched, unresolved or missing result. Standalone PR-mode `/prflow:review-and-fix` runs keep the checkout. (#2047)
- **`/prflow:spec` states which checks can show a reported bug is already gone.** Before it recommends *No change — file nothing*, this run's initial documentation and code checks must positively show each failure in your bug report gone; a failure the run merely did not reproduce does not count. When those checks fall back to a reduced inline check, its results can still count, and the evidence PRFlow gives you says the check was reduced. (#1978)

## October 8, 2026

- **`/prflow:spec` now asks "Assign this issue to you?" and, when offered, whether to start implementation together with the approval question, before the issue is created.** On a runner that asks one question at a time, they come right after you approve. After creation PRFlow applies the answers and asks nothing more, so you can approve and walk away.
- **`/prflow:spec` states each quality group's routing trigger once and owes the skipped-step case for every new or changed gate.** The quality-group rows of the degradation-routing table now point at the root's *Advanced quality-guidance routing* bullet instead of restating its triggers, the issue template's Current Behavior and Technical Context guidance no longer restates them, and the group files drop their shared intro sentences. The guarantee-class case — a deterministic hook, gate or backstop fires when the cooperative step it backs was skipped, idempotently where enforcement repeats — moves from the regression group to the contracts group, which every such draft loads. (#1852)
