- **`/prflow:spec` saves the investigation record beside the draft and posts it in one step.** The approval message now shows the record's file path instead of printing the whole record, and *Print the full draft in chat* prints the record after the body. The record file is saved even when `spec.investigation_record_enabled` is `false`; that setting now stops only the comment, and the file is removed with the run's scratch once the issue is filed. Publishing the record takes one helper call, and `/prflow:implement` no longer reads the posted record as an issue comment. (#1868)
- **`/prflow:spec`, `/prflow:init` and `/prflow:retrospective-weekly` report a refused prompt-extension load as unestablished.** A load that prints no `PROMPT-EXTENSION-STATUS:` line on stderr, as after the client refuses the command, is now reported instead of being treated as no extension, as the skill-extensions documentation already describes. (#1964)
- **Spec-filed issues are shorter.** The `/prflow:spec` issue template no longer adds a fixed scope note to Technical Context. It also drops the Technical Context file list and `Dependencies` bullet, and leaves out a Technical Context bullet that has nothing to say instead of writing "none". Files are listed once, in Implementation Notes' `Relevant files`, which opens with `at minimum`. Retrospective-audit and deferral follow-up issues follow the same shape. (#1837)
- **`/prflow:spec` can end with nothing filed.** When a verified check from this run's Step 1 shows the current tree no longer produces any failure a reported defect names, the implementation-approach question is asked before every other clarification question except whether to widen an existing issue, and recommends *No change — file nothing*; choosing it ends the run at Step 2 with nothing written to GitHub, and the outcome gives the evidence and names the open issues left for you to close (#1951).
- **A review verdict that fails to post now reads as undelivered.** When both the review and the comment POST fail (`FAILED no-durable-channel`), `post-review-verdict.sh` no longer stamps the verdict marker on the progress comment, and `derive-review-verdict.sh` reads a progress comment's verdict only from that marker, so the run derives `incomplete`. Once the installed workflow and vendored helpers are both current (re-run the installer with the new tag), a cloud `/prflow:review` run that was not cancelled fails its job on such a post, and the review stall backstop re-requests the review as it does after an engine error. (#1965)
- **`/prflow:spec` no longer rebuilds a lost working-draft file from memory.** A failed write or edit of the working-draft file that is not a permission refusal or filesystem failure is re-read and retried once, and the draft moves to the chat message only when the first Write is refused or still fails. (#1946)
- **`/prflow:spec`'s Step 3.5 self-audit runs one omission pass and one revision.** Item 5 is the only revision. The old item 6 self-check is gone and the summary moved from item 7 to item 6, so a spec skill extension that cites Step 3.5 items by number needs updating. The drafting rules for mechanical claims, occurrence counts, data-entity and replaced-gate reads, file references and multi-state contracts now live in the issue template. (#1819)
- **Checklist verification is faster and cheaper.** Each checklist verifier now reads one item file that carries its source views, its verdict file and only the grading rules its claim needs, so every verifier loads less prose and the review no longer retypes revisions and rules into each dispatch. A verifier that answers without writing its verdict file no longer holds the verification wave for nine minutes after the other verifiers finish. Checklist batches are sized by diff size rather than a fixed ten files, so a large pull request with small changes uses fewer generators. (#1797, #1791, #1782)
- **A local review no longer idles after its checklist generators finish.** Phase 1 now ends its generator dispatch with one wait on the batch files, which returns as soon as they exist instead of sitting out a nine-minute deadline. (#1783)
- **The checklist deduper and lite verification are gone.** Cross-batch duplicates are now merged by identical claim signature without an extra agent, and no claim is settled by a string probe in place of a verifier. A `prflow:checklist-deduper` or `devflow:checklist-deduper` entry in `prflow_review.agent_overrides` still validates but is ignored, so you can delete it.
- **A claim that a path does not exist is settled from the reviewed commit's file list.** A verifier no longer leaves such a claim inconclusive for want of a deleted-file record. A checklist item left inconclusive because a file could not be read now caps the verdict at APPROVE WITH CAVEAT. (#1440)
- **Helper entry points the review-and-fix loop no longer calls are removed: a caller now gets exit 2, or 127 when it runs a deleted script directly.**
  - `load-prompt-extension.sh --provenance`, `--diff-patch` and `--since`: an unrecognized-argument error.
  - `loop-verdict-marker.py compose`, `eval-extension-shadow-trigger` and `write-active-entry-binding`, and the `--entry` and `--head` options of `check-evidence`: an argparse usage error. `check-evidence --iteration` now requires `--contract 2`.
  - `review-dirty-tree.sh entry-open` and `entry-close` without `--contract 3`: refused.
  - `lib/efficiency-trace.sh --mode`, with any value: refused; `--persist` and `--self-check` are unchanged.
  - `scripts/stale-prose-lint.py` and `scripts/match-lint-adjudications.py` are deleted: `python3 <path>` exits 2, a direct call 127 (not found).
  - `scripts/check-completion-evidence.py` has no command line: run as a command it exits 2. `/prflow:implement`'s completion gate, which imports it, is unchanged.
- **A prompt extension can no longer declare an early shadow trigger.** The shadow review runs at convergence only, and `.prflow/skill-extensions/early-shadow-path-set.json` is no longer read. An extension that still describes such a trigger is read as plain review policy. (#956)
- **`workpad.py --review-coverage-disposition` no longer accepts the `extension-provenance` cause class.** A disposition that names it is refused as `[review-coverage-cause-inadmissible]`, with no workpad edit.
- **Workflow allowlists no longer grant the three removed scripts.** The generated `TOOLS` lists drop `check-completion-evidence.py`, `stale-prose-lint.py` and `match-lint-adjudications.py`; re-run `install.sh` to refresh an installed workflow. A workflow that still lists them keeps working.
- **A file a review subagent creates no longer stops a standalone `/prflow:review-and-fix` run.** The loop still resets a subagent's edits to tracked files before fixing; it lists both kinds in its output and never commits them. Under `/prflow:implement` such a file still blocks the run after the loop.
- **The loop applies the pull request's own `.prflow/skill-extensions/` policy, with no provenance check.** Protect `.prflow/skill-extensions/` with a CODEOWNERS entry so extension edits need an owner's review.
- **A shorter loop exit.** The loop no longer prints a telemetry table, per-iteration finding counts or an effectiveness trace, runs the completion-evidence check, or downgrades a final REJECT, and a clean gate writes no workpad reflection. A standalone `--push-each-iteration` run no longer re-runs the test suite at loop exit after merging the base branch; CI on the pushed head checks the merge.
- **A finding pushed back in two consecutive iterations no longer prints "Finding persists after pushback".**
- **`prflow_review.stale_prose.enabled` and `.severity` stay accepted and do nothing.** A config that sets them still validates.
- **The loop's `deferrals.json` no longer carries `default_channel`.**
- **A shadow review that fails before writing its evidence now ends the loop as not verified** instead of stopping it.
- **The review-fix worker can check claims about external tools on the web.** `prflow:review-fix-worker` now has WebFetch and WebSearch.
- **`/prflow:spec` audit rounds read the auditor's own return instead of a hand copy.** When you elect an audit round, the auditor now writes its complete return — verdict, draft identity check and per-finding evidence — to the run's audit report file, and the round is read straight from that file. A round takes fewer orchestration turns and less copied output, and the findings quoted to you are the auditor's own. Runs that elect no audit round see no change. (#1748)
- **`/prflow:review-and-fix` now protects uncommitted edits in files you were already changing when a review agent touches them.** Each engine entry records the content of every tracked file; when that record is available, closing the entry puts back each tracked file outside `.prflow/tmp/` that the engine edited, staged or discarded, except a submodule checkout it moves without staging, a file marked assume-unchanged or skip-worktree, and an edit that line-ending conversion or a clean filter normalizes away. A file the engine creates is only unstaged, and a deletion the engine undoes stops the loop rather than deleting the file again (a staged deletion only when the engine also stages the file; a staged new file you deleted only while the entry's `git status` snapshot is usable, without which the file is recreated with its staged content). When the record cannot be made (for example, an intent-to-add entry exists when the review starts), the loop falls back to its earlier behavior: an engine change to a file you had already modified is not undone, and is named only when the file's `git status` changed. Before resetting, when git can, the loop saves the content it overwrites and names the saved object in its report, so `git checkout <id> -- <path>` recovers it until git prunes the object.
- **A re-review grades a previous finding against the finding itself.** When `/prflow:review` re-checks a finding from the previous review that quotes no text still in the code, it now checks the finding's own words instead of a generated restatement, so a misworded restatement can no longer fail a defect you already fixed. (#1992)
- **Implement-phase agents that hold Bash no longer prefer Grep and Glob tools a local run refuses.** Implement-phase agents that hold Bash (intake, branch setup, issue-claim audit, evidence verification and finalization) replace their instruction to prefer Grep and Glob tools with the reviewer agents' instruction to search through Bash `grep`/`rg` or a search tool the agent holds. (#1790)
- **`/prflow:review-and-fix`'s deferrals manifest holds every iteration's standing deferral.** Loop Exit builds `deferrals.json` with `loop-verdict-marker.py build-deferrals` from every iteration's decisions, not only the final one's, leaving out a deferral a later iteration fixed or decided again, and applies the widens-surface rule `/prflow:review`'s deferral matcher uses. `/prflow:implement` files its follow-up issues from that manifest.
- **The final report's `## Coverage` section lists every checklist FAIL and INCONCLUSIVE item** of the last iteration that ran the checklist, marking a FAIL that iteration then fixed.
- **The fix loop uses `/prflow:fix`'s fix rules and its `prflow:fix-delta-reviewer`.** When the loop cannot dispatch `prflow:fix-delta-reviewer`, it records `fix-delta not verified` instead of running a `general-purpose` stand-in, and the report's `## Coverage` section names the gap; the shadow pass stays the backstop, so the verdict is unchanged.
- **Every reviewer sees the acceptance criteria and, from iteration 2, the earlier findings.** The loop passes the issue and the iteration to the review engine on every entry and, from iteration 2, a prior-findings file to each Step 1 entry; the shadow pass still sees no earlier findings.
- **Standalone `/prflow:review` no longer adds `suspected over-grade` notes.** The fix loop still calibrates over-graded findings before promoting them.
- **Inside `/prflow:implement`, a review engine that cannot dispatch its reviewers stops the run with a remedy.** Launch `/prflow:implement` at the top level, or raise the subagent nesting limit: in Claude Code set `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` to 4; in VS Code Copilot turn on `chat.subagents.allowInvocationsFromSubagents`. A standalone `/prflow:review-and-fix` still runs the engine inline.
- **New helper subcommands and contract.** `loop-verdict-marker.py build-deferrals` and `render-exit`; `review-dirty-tree.sh entry-open` and `entry-close` take `--contract 3`, which adds the `prior` and `engine_return` fields, and refuse an earlier contract.

## October 7, 2026

- **A review checks an approval against its checklist and reviewer records before posting it.** `/prflow:review` now refuses an approve-family verdict while a checklist FAIL counts against your `verdict_severity_threshold`, and posts REJECT instead. It also refuses one while a reviewer the run planned, the final pass included, left no record of having run; the review then ends without a verdict, naming what was missing, and no longer re-runs reviewers itself — re-run the review. Local reviews of a pull request are checked the same way as cloud ones. A REJECT is checked too, for the reviewers every review runs, and ends without a verdict when one of them left no record. Once a verdict posts, the posting step ticks the progress comment's last row and, for an approval, clears PRFlow's own stale change requests. When the posting step posts nothing (both of its channels fail, it refuses an argument, or it prints nothing), the progress comment's status reads `❌ <verdict> not posted` with the reason; on a run with no progress comment the report now reaches the run's chat output only, where before the review also posted it as a plain pull request comment. If your repository commits a vendored copy of PRFlow, re-vendor it with this update: until you do, a local review cannot render its checklist, Deferrals or Issue Compliance sections, so it approves at most with a caveat, and posts its verdict unchecked with the whole progress report as the review body, leaves the last row unticked and clears no stale change request. (#1656)
- **Deferrals listed in a pull request body no longer lower a finding's weight.** The review report's `## Deferrals` section still lists each deferral, and for one that matches a current finding now says whether that finding was filed at or above your threshold.
- **Helper-rendered report sections.** The checklist results and issue-compliance sections are now produced by PRFlow's helpers rather than written out by the model; the issue-compliance line names the issue by number, without its title. When the progress comment holds the report, a cloud review's chat output is the verdict line and a pointer to that comment instead of the whole report; a local review still prints the full report.
- **`/prflow:init` now sets `prflow.effort` to `medium`.** Cloud reviews run below `medium` skipped review steps more often. The setting applies to every cloud command except implementation, not only reviews, and to the weekly retrospective when `prflow_retrospective.effort` is unset, so those runs cost more than at `low`. Existing configs keep their value.
- **The final-pass reviewer is now the `prflow:requesting-code-review` agent.** The review engine dispatches it like its other reviewers and loads your `.prflow/skill-extensions/requesting-code-review.md` itself, passing the text to the reviewer and reporting the extension's load status in the review. Its `prflow_review.agent_overrides` key keeps working, and `/prflow:requesting-code-review` still runs the same reviewer on demand.
- **Review agents share one findings contract.** All six reviewers grade findings on the same Critical, Important and Suggestion scale, set out at the end of each reviewer's instructions; an untrue line is still graded by who reads it. Five of the six reviewers keep severity rules of their own on top of it. The comment and type-design reviewers now report severities on that scale in place of their own categories and 1–10 ratings. Reviewers run no mutation checks and none of the project's tests; they verify a claim about a test by reading its source.
- **Reviewers search with `grep` or `rg` and skip the command-shapes read.** Reviewer instructions no longer direct a Grep tool call or a read of the command-shapes file. (#1790, #1201)
- **A deferral in a pull request body can no longer hide the rest of the review report.** The report's `## Deferrals` section escapes an HTML comment opener (`<!--`) in every field it shows, so text such as a deferral id no longer comments out the sections after it. A deferrals block that is present but cannot be read now says why in place of zero counts.
- **The review requested when CI passes is no longer skipped as a duplicate.** When a new commit was pushed while an earlier review was running, that review could move to the new commit before its CI finished, and the review PRFlow requests once that commit's CI passed was then skipped as a duplicate. A review whose progress comment shows it running no longer swallows that request. Two reviews of one commit may occasionally overlap. (#1490)
- **A deferrals block with no END marker after its START marker is now reported as unreadable** in the report's `## Deferrals` section. Before, an END marker placed only before the START marker stopped the review's deferral matcher, and a START marker with no END marker anywhere was read as no block.
- **The spec skill's implementation-approach question is written in plain words.** Its recommendation now says what the supporting check found, and the question says what the run could not check or ruled out without checking, instead of naming internal evidence labels or counting skipped entries. When nothing checked supports a recommendation, the question says so plainly. (#1858)
- **On macOS and Windows, a review no longer stops at engine setup when the repo tracks two paths whose names differ only in letter case.** The review's source view records the names the filesystem stores as one (`readme` beside `README`, `foo` beside `FOO/x`) as unread `path-too-long` entries instead of stopping with `view-path` or `view-write`; when both are files, the earlier one is left out too, so neither name is read as the other's bytes. A harness `.src` rename onto a tracked `.src` file, and a root name stored as `inventory.json`, still stop as `view-path`.
- **`/prflow:implement` now has the agent record every skip its final suite run reported, so a run whose suite skipped a test ends Blocked instead of Complete.** Phase 4.3 tells the agent to list each skip the suite's output reports in the verification summary, pre-existing ones included, and no longer presents an empty skip list as the requirement.
- **Implement PR descriptions no longer report a stale CI or test-suite status.** The PR description written near the end of an implement run is now checked for sentences reporting whether CI checks or the test suite passed, failed or are still running, and a stale or unsupported one is corrected. A Test Plan step naming a check to run is left as written. (#1424)
- **`/prflow:implement` no longer dispatches the code-architect because of a change's size alone.** It dispatches the architect only when a structural design decision is still open — the issue does not prescribe it, or discovery contradicts what it prescribes — or when that cannot be established; every other change is planned inline, however many files it touches. (#1778)
- **The weekly retrospective no longer audits or files a pattern that has gone quiet.** A pattern is sent to Stage B, and can be filed, only when one of its occurrences merged at or after the earliest merge among the PRs the run scanned, or when the run cannot establish a merge time that decides this. (#1410)
- **Search fallbacks no longer miss hidden directories or walk sibling worktrees.** The docs skills, `/prflow:fix` and implement's Phase 2 sweeps now search with the Grep tool, else `git grep --untracked -nP` over the whole repository. The old `rg` rung skipped hidden directories such as `.github/`, and the old `grep -rnE` rung walked sibling worktrees and could stall past the Bash timeout. Implement's sweeps count matches with `git grep -c` instead of `rg` or `grep`, and their cross-line phrase search uses the Grep tool's multiline mode, else `rg -U --hidden`, replacing the `tr` form. A git built without PCRE fails the `git grep` rung loudly (exit 128) instead of returning no matches.
- **review-and-fix: fix-delta gate Suggestions now reach the fixer when your threshold admits them.** With `fix_severity_threshold: suggestion`, a Suggestion or Minor finding from the Step 3.5 fix-delta gate was always parked as advisory, so a defect the gate had already spotted could come back as a PR-review REJECT. It now routes the way the iteration's other findings of that severity route, and is re-fixed and re-gated in the same iteration under the gate's existing two-attempt cap. Repositories on the default `important` or on `critical` see no change. (#1704)
- **`/prflow:implement` no longer writes a workpad row for a check that found nothing to act on.** A passing dependency preflight, a clean issue-claim audit pass, a CI-verdict read that listed at least one run and whose every group passed with no skipped job, a docs pass with no changes, and a Phase 4.2 claim-audit class that found no false claim now write no workpad row of their own; findings, failures and checkpoint records are kept. (#1693)
- **A later `/prflow:spec` audit round now counts as a full audit of the draft.** When you elect a second or third audit round, the audit summary now reports that latest round's finding counts instead of an earlier round's. A clean later round no longer triggers an extra automatic round you did not ask for. (#1747)
- **`/prflow:spec` re-checks the draft after each change.** `/prflow:spec` now writes the draft to a working-draft file in the run directory, and the verified-premise check and the acceptance-criteria parseability gate re-read it after each change — so a fix those checks call for passes the no-options gate and revision-delta verification, and a draft revised at the Step 4 review is parsed again before it is filed.
- **`/prflow:spec` no longer writes its Testing Strategy coverage-sweep cases into Acceptance Criteria.** A sweep case becomes a criterion only when the criterion grade adds or merges it; otherwise it stays a Testing Strategy case. The Testing Strategy guidance in the issue template is also shorter. (#1838)

## October 6, 2026

- **`/prflow:spec` leaves decisions an implementer can clearly make to the implementer.** `/prflow:spec` no longer asks about, or writes into the issue, a decision you left open that a competent implementer could clearly make from your request and the codebase, unless the issue lists it as one item of a complete set; the implementer makes it and the pull-request review judges it. It still asks which implementation approach to take, and asks whenever it is unclear whether an implementer could decide. When a rule sorts cases that cannot all be listed, such as the scope of a change, the issue states it once as the rule, which way it fails when a case is unclear, and the limit it accepts, and every check, the fresh-context audit included, accepts that instead of asking for more cases; a set whose members can all be listed is still listed member by member. A revision now fixes what produced a finding across the whole draft, not only the line the finding names. Issues come out shorter and audit rounds stop adding one missed case at a time. (#1806)
- **Reviews no longer block a pull request on an inaccurate code comment or internal doc.** An untrue code comment, docstring or repository-internal doc page is now reported as a Suggestion. Customer-facing prose such as a README, a published doc page or a release note is reported as Important at most. Neither one REJECTs the pull request at the default threshold. An untrue line that a tool or agent acts on, such as a skill body or a lint directive, still blocks as before, and a finding that the code misses a case it should cover is still graded on that gap, wherever the gap is described.
- **Run evidence and cloud cost records are kept even with the effectiveness record turned off.** Each run's JSON workpad files now reach the telemetry branch (a run dir whose name is an unfilled placeholder is still refused), including a standalone review's findings and checklist, which were dropped when the run had no iteration record. Setting `prflow_review_and_fix.efficiency_telemetry_enabled` to false now stops only the effectiveness record (and the data synthesized to feed it) and denied-command records: cloud runs keep recording their cost and run profile, and only `telemetry.enabled: false` stops those. The weekly retrospective's trailing four-week cost and duration lines now say when the last figure was recorded instead of presenting older weeks as current, a regression line compares a week only with the four calendar weeks before it, and its cost ranking no longer counts standalone review runs as fix-loop iterations. Upgrade note: in a repository with `efficiency_telemetry_enabled` false, the next writable run copies any leftover run files (findings, checklists, prior comments) and cloud cost records to the telemetry branch, which anyone who can read the repository can read; set `telemetry.enabled` to false to keep them off it. (#1808)
- **Reviews start faster.** One helper call now gathers a review's diff and related issue, plus a pull request's refs and description when there is one, including for a standalone review of a pull request number. A local `/prflow:review-and-fix` run now keeps one progress comment across its iterations. The stale-prose check no longer runs. `prflow_review.stale_prose.enabled` and `severity` still validate but are ignored. A per-agent `effort` in `prflow_review.agent_overrides` was never applied and is now ignored, with no notice; every review agent runs at the session effort. `/prflow:init` no longer scaffolds either setting. (#1792, #1794)
- **Fix: `/prflow:create-issue` now runs exactly like `/prflow:spec`.** The alias hands its arguments to `/prflow:spec` and runs it as its own skill. Before, the alias read the spec instructions as a file and added its own setup rules. Those rules could stop a run that `/prflow:spec` would have continued, and the user story reached spec only indirectly. `/prflow:create-issue` and `/devflow:create-issue` are permanent aliases, and the docs no longer call them transitional. (#1826)
- **`/prflow:spec` no longer checks its scratch files before showing the draft.** The approval message no longer carries two `path=… class=…` lines, and a missing scratch file no longer re-runs the docs check or the derivation pass. `scripts/cleanup-spec-run.sh --probe-run-state` is removed. (#1824)
- **`/prflow:spec` asks one visual question for a UI change instead of two.** When an issue changes what users see and you have not already shared a screenshot or mockup, the spec run now asks once: attach a screenshot or mockup, or confirm the proposed visual details (layout, states, responsive behavior, style). It no longer asks for a screenshot first and then follows up on the details. Non-UI issues still get no visual question. (#1853)
- **`/prflow:spec` now reports when it could not add the `PRFlow` label to a new issue.** The run's final summary names the label as not applied, with the reason. (#1869)
- **`/prflow:fix` is shorter and stops on a wrong checkout.** Its body is about a fifth of its former size. On a pull request it fetches, then stops before changing anything unless it can read the pull request, the working tree is clean and you are on the pull request's head or ahead of it. It also stops when it cannot tell whether the branch has a pull request, or when a bare number in front of the feedback is not the current branch's pull request. The eleven-fact preflight block and the completion-evidence check are gone from the pass, which now reports each finding as fixed, pushed back or deferred with its evidence, plus the local test result, the fix-delta gate line and a branch-sync measurement. When the local test run is denied, it reads the pull request's checks only if the pull request's head is the commit holding every fix; otherwise it reports the tests as unverified and does not claim completion. The `receiving_review.fix_severity_threshold` setting keeps its values and default; an array or object there now counts as unset.
- **Update prompt extensions that name removed `/prflow:fix` sections.** Every `##` section of the old body is gone, among them the Reception Preflight, Update the Branch First (Step 0), Verification Gate (Step 8) and Record Every Deferral, so a `.prflow/skill-extensions/fix.md` that points at one of them now points at nothing; point it at a step's heading or a fix-discipline section name instead. An extension or script that calls `reception-record.py` changes too: it no longer accepts `append-disposition`, `--token` or `--session-dir`.
- **A fix makes the smallest edit that closes its finding.** Whatever the severity, `/prflow:fix` deletes the faulty code or text or makes the smallest closing edit, and adds new text or a new code path only when the finding, or a rule the fix triggers, needs it. The rule lives in `skills/fix/references/fix-discipline.md`. (#1770)
- **`/prflow:fix` no longer stalls on an unclear finding.** The pass skips that finding and any finding it may affect, records the open question as the deferral, and fixes the rest. (#1657)
- **The direct-pass fix-delta review is a named agent.** `/prflow:fix` now reviews its own fixes through the new `fix-delta-reviewer` agent, which computes the fix delta itself and returns one line per finding; how the pass routes those findings is unchanged. Where that agent type cannot be dispatched, the gate line reads `not verified`.
- **`/prflow:spec` loads less text when it drafts an issue.** The issue template's checklist, which repeated rules the template already states, is now one self-check sentence. The run no longer records a disposition line for each acceptance criterion, so the approval prompt no longer shows a disposition note beside the criterion count. (#1836)
- **`/prflow:spec` tracks its progress in your runner's own task tool.** The run now uses whatever task-tracking tool your runner offers, whatever its name. A run with no task tool keeps its checklist in the conversation and no longer writes a checklist file. The first line of the run says which tracker is in use. (#1827)
- **`/prflow:spec` asks before rewriting an existing issue.** It widens an open issue only when your request names it or, after its duplicate search finds one, you choose to widen it; a non-interactive run never widens an issue you did not name and, when it goes on, files a new issue and names the suspected duplicate. On a widen, the approval question says that approving replaces the issue's title and body, and a confirmed widen tries to register the new body's declared prerequisites as blocked-by links, naming any it could not link. A run that files or widens says in its final outcome when the duplicate search could not run. (#1831)
- **`/prflow:spec` no longer writes a Steelman record or a `steelman-projection-<slug>.json` file, and Step 3.6 entry and the Step 4 presentation gate no longer read them back.** Step 3.5 reports its summary in chat only. A change requested at the approval pause is checked by Revision-delta verification alone instead of re-running Step 3.5 (it now also fails a revision that leaves a Desired Behavior obligation with no acceptance criterion); `kept at fork:` lines are still recorded in the derivation artifact. A spec prompt extension that names the removed record or JSON file should stop naming them. (#1817)

## October 5, 2026

- **`/prflow:docs-verify --report-only` no longer returns a status per duty.** Its last report field, **Duty statuses**, is replaced by **Not established**: each duty the run did not carry out or could not establish, and each internal-documentation page it located but did not read in full, with a one-clause reason each, or `none`. `/prflow:spec` Step 1 copies that field into its evidence file and no longer checks the documentation lead's location against its own resolution. A consumer extension or caller that names duty statuses now names a field that no longer exists.
- **`/prflow:spec` reports a config-withheld investigation record plainly.** `/prflow:spec`: with `spec.investigation_record_enabled` set to `false`, the final outcome reports only that the investigation record was withheld by config; it no longer names a `Considered-and-rejected:` line as lost.
- **`/prflow:spec` widens replace the issue's title along with its body.** The approved draft's title goes in the same request as the body, instead of the old title staying in place.
- **`/prflow:spec` keeps mechanisms and heuristic case lists out of acceptance criteria.** A mechanism you did not ask for goes in Implementation Notes unless another surface reads it as a contract, and a heuristic's criterion states its rule, which way it fails and its limit. (#1752)
- **`/prflow:retrospective-weekly` now sends each recurring category to Stage B once per run.** When several actionable patterns outside cooldown share a category, only the first-ranked one is dispatched; the others read "not filed" in the report, and a notice in the run output names them. The `--full` pattern view and every record's status are unchanged.
- **`/prflow:review-and-fix` now links each fix decision and deferral to the finding it acts on**, so a decision can no longer be attributed to a different finding. When it skips a checklist failure on a file the PR changes beyond comments, the skip no longer downgrades a REJECT. (#1751)
- **Cloud CI verification no longer dispatches CI for a commit that is not checked out.** `ci-verification-request.py request` now refuses a head SHA that differs from the checkout's current commit, naming that commit, before it runs any pre-request check or dispatches CI. It also refuses when the current commit cannot be read. A mistyped SHA now costs one quick retry instead of a failed CI run on the pull request. (#1773)
- `/prflow:retrospective-weekly` stores every record with the repository its pull request belongs to again, so patterns built from analyzed pull requests reach Stage B instead of being refused because their occurrences name no repository. When the weekly run merges new records into the learnings store, every record that names no repository, new or already stored, gains the run's repository and, when its pull request number is an integer, its `pr_key`. When it updates stored records it reports their count on stderr, and when a record needs the run's repository but that repository cannot be resolved, it stores nothing. A pull request analyzed again ends with one record of that kind, replacing every stored record it matches. The scan's warning about records that name no repository now says the next merge gives them the run's repository instead of advising a migration script. (#1765)

## October 4, 2026

- **Review-and-fix re-checks an earlier fix before undoing it.** Before a fix deletes or rewrites text, the fixer checks that it does not bring back a finding about that file that an earlier iteration of the same run fixed, and reworks the edit so both stay fixed. When both can't hold, the later fix is not made and its finding is pushed back. (#1695)

## October 2, 2026

- **Native-Windows paths no longer break `/prflow:spec`'s audit or `/prflow:implement`'s setup.** On native Windows, helpers now print paths with forward slashes, so a path pasted into a Git Bash command names a real file. Printed paths on Linux, macOS and WSL are unchanged. (#1665)
- **Fix: `/prflow:implement` no longer risks stopping as Blocked after a clean review or finalization.** The check that reads each worker's result printed nothing when a review-fix or finalization result passed, and a check that prints nothing is how a refused command looks, so a successful run could be stopped as Blocked. That check now prints the passing result's outcome, for example `{"outcome":"proceed"}`, on every pass. A failing result is reported as before. You get this through the normal plugin update. (#1699)
- **`/prflow:implement`'s acceptance-criteria gate writes a smaller workpad record.** Each Phase 3.4 pass now records the tally and one line for each criterion the gate does not tick; when every criterion is ticked, or there are none, the record is the tally line alone. The pass no longer writes a note naming its scratch attempt directory, and tick calls carry no note. The verifier's evidence for a ticked criterion no longer reaches the issue. (#1530)
- **`/prflow:implement` files only real action items under the workpad's "⚠️ Action required".** When the review-fix loop soft-proceeds, a leftover finding graded below Important is now a note under "ℹ️ Notes"; an Important one stays under "Action required". A finding the run declined because it would weaken an acceptance criterion is now recorded as an "Issue accuracy" note, and the PR body's `Disputed criterion` line is unchanged. (#1698)
- **A page your issue's Documentation Needed note only points at no longer blocks a finished `/prflow:implement` run.** In a line such as `` `docs/guide.md`: link to `docs/setup.md` ``, the text after the colon now describes the edit and is not read as another file to edit, so `docs/setup.md` is no longer a required deliverable and is no longer reported as a refused deliverable. Files named before the colon, or outside any such description, are still required. The issue template now tells writers to name by path only the files the change edits. (#1691)
- **A criterion is tagged post-merge only by an exact ` (post-merge)` ending or an unambiguous phrase.** An acceptance criterion that names a `post-merge` or `post-deploy` flag, path or file — such as `--exclude-post-merge` or a `.husky/post-merge` hook — is no longer tagged post-merge and stays in implement's merge gate. A criterion is tagged only when it ends in exactly ` (post-merge)`, lowercase, or uses a multi-word phrase such as "after merge" or "on a live PR". `(post-deploy)`, `(Post-Merge)`, `[post-merge]` and a criterion that says only "verify post-merge that …" are no longer tagged; end such a criterion in ` (post-merge)` to keep it out of the merge gate. (#1700)
- **`/prflow:spec`'s investigation-record comment no longer carries the run's raw working notes.** The first comment on a spec-filed issue is now the investigation record PRFlow sorted out of the body, plus one `Considered-and-rejected:` line when the run passed over heavier approaches. The criterion disposition, steelman, self-audit and evidence-bundle sections are no longer appended: they were written before later revisions, could contradict the final issue body, and made up most of the comment. A record over 65,536 bytes, a conservative bound on GitHub's comment limit, is not posted rather than cut. (#1669)
- **A first-pass restate no longer makes `implement`'s acceptance-criteria verifiers grade a criterion alone.** The verifiers now treat a dispatch as a re-verification pass only when it carries the exact line `This is a re-verification pass.`, so a restate, rerun or redispatch request without it still lets sibling criteria and extra coverage excuse a criterion, instead of costing a fix round. (#1507)
- **`/prflow:spec` questions keep their background under a terse output style.** Every clarification question now opens with one or two sentences on what the answer decides and what it touches, even when your output style asks for no preamble; a chat message before the questions may add more but never replaces it. Before its next question, or before drafting when none follows, the run also names, one line each, every decision it settled without asking that your story does not state, so you can contest it before it reaches the draft. (#1660)
- **`/prflow:spec` also writes an Implementation Notes "no X" or size-cap decision as an acceptance criterion.** Only a criterion has standing against a review finding, so for an issue spec writes, the review-and-fix loop's existing criterion-conflict decline now covers such a decision. Spec also checks each criterion against the Implementation Notes and reconciles a conflict before filing the issue; a decision that cannot be a criterion is removed from the Notes. Hand-written issues are unchanged. (#1696)
- **Cloud `/prflow:implement` runs get through the documentation pass's deliverable and config reads as written.** Phase 4.1 now runs both Documentation Needed reads and the six docs-config reads through the installed `.prflow/vendor/prflow/` helpers first, which the cloud tier allows, and falls back to the plugin path when that copy cannot run. (#1539)
- **One malformed `allowed_tools` entry no longer silently drops every extra tool grant on a cloud run.** The cloud config job now keeps each `prflow.allowed_tools` or `prflow_implement.allowed_tools` entry that is a non-empty single-line string and skips the rest with a warning naming the key, each skipped index and its JSON type. A non-null value that is not an array grants nothing and also warns. Entries that used to pass through are now skipped: numbers, booleans, and the values of an object written in place of the array. Entries containing a line break can no longer write extra lines into the job's outputs. Takes effect after you re-run `install.sh --apply`, which refreshes the config action and the retrospective workflow. (#1435)
- **The `/prflow:spec` issue template now says where a Documentation Needed description ends.** The text after `` `docs/guide.md`: `` can end before the end of the line, for example at `;`, `. ` or the next `` `path`: ``. Put a page the change only points at before that point, or describe it without its path. (#1723)
- **A malformed review finding no longer crashes the deferral match.** A malformed review finding — one that is not an object, or whose line range is not two whole line numbers in order — no longer crashes the review's deferral match, and your other deferrals are still matched. A deferral whose line range is reversed is now rejected as malformed instead of matching a finding. (#1554)
- **An acceptance criterion keeps its indented paragraph after a blank line.** When a checkbox criterion continues with an indented paragraph or nested list after a blank line, `/prflow:implement` now mirrors, gates and reviews the whole criterion instead of silently cutting it off at the blank line. A non-indented line or the next checkbox still ends it, and post-merge trigger phrases match across the whole joined criterion. (#1715)

## October 1, 2026

- **`/prflow:spec` counts an item verified only when a run-time read confirms it.** `/prflow:spec` now states one definition of "verified": an item counts only when a read made during the run covers its locator in the file as it still stands and confirms it. The Step 3.5 record and the revision-delta evidence line count only such items and name each other item unverified. The facts an adopted edit introduces are enumerated from the edit's replacement text, and a fact list supplied with the edit is treated as a starting point. `issue-audit-state.py record-adjudication` now refuses a round that holds fewer finding-evidence records than findings (`finding-evidence-count`). On a round with findings, `record-return` now points its `next_call=` line at `record-finding-evidence`, and `record-finding-evidence` points its line at `query-finding-evidence`.
- **`/prflow:spec` asks before a draft makes code parse the layout of Markdown a model writes.** Such code now reads only the parts the producer marks for machines by default; parsing headings, section order or bullet shapes becomes a question to the user, recorded as blocked on a run with no user. (#1557)
- **`/prflow:spec` Step 4 loads only the post-approval steps its run takes.** `/prflow:spec` Step 4 now loads only the post-approval steps its run takes: filing a new issue or widening an existing one loads `skills/spec/references/step-4-create.md`, read alongside the approval re-query, so every pre-approval turn carries less text. Sub-step 3a now asks its decision question in the same reply that shows the audit summary line, the investigation record and the draft path, with the question last.
- **Review and review-and-fix no longer hold a pull request at REJECT on a checklist item's own error.** A re-review's seed from the prior report is now re-checked against the reviewed head's text rather than an excerpt copied from an earlier round, so a fix the review prescribed stops re-failing. A confirmed source defect and an unmet acceptance criterion still weigh at their severity.
- **New `/prflow:help` command troubleshoots a PRFlow problem.** It asks what you ran and what went wrong, checks your PRFlow version against the newest release, other installed copies, the environment and `gh` sign-in, `.prflow/config.json`, the vendored copy, a failed cloud run's log, and — for a local session — the model and effort level against the recommendations published at `https://prflow.ai/docs/configuration/recommended-models-and-effort`. It gives one verdict: setup problem (with the fix), likely PRFlow bug, or undetermined. Only a likely bug, or an undetermined case you confirm, gets a Markdown report under `.prflow/tmp/help/` for you to review and share; the command posts nothing anywhere.
- **`/prflow:spec` checks comparisons between two runs.** A drafted criterion or test that compares one run's output with another's is now grounded like a comparison with a fixed value, and must name the other run and the input both runs take. (#1597)
- **The weekly retrospective saves its learnings to the telemetry branch instead of opening a state pull request.** Its records (`retrospectives.jsonl`, `experiment-records.jsonl`, `overrides.json`) and each run's report now live under `.prflow/logs/learnings/` on the telemetry branch. A run loads them into the untracked `.prflow/learnings/` working copy, saves them before filing issues and again at the end, and opens no pull request. This also fixes a stale read: the run used to check out the default branch after opening its state pull request, so the filing caps and the report read last week's files. A save refuses, pushing nothing, when someone else changed the stored records during the run; when the first save does not land, refused or failed, the run files no issue and the report says why. `retro-helper.sh dismiss <pattern-key>` now stops a recurring pattern. `/prflow:init` and `install.sh --apply` copy still-tracked learnings files to the branch and stage their removal for you to commit; a tracked file that differs from records already on the branch, or has uncommitted changes, stops them, staging nothing. The scheduled workflow no longer skips a week while a state pull request is open, appends the report to the job summary, and drops `lib/open-state-pr.sh`, `lib/post-status.sh` and `scripts/retrospective-state-guard.sh`. Bump `prflow_version` and re-run `install.sh` in the same upgrade. (#1511)
- **`/prflow:spec` offers to split a feature whose parts could ship separately.** When one feature's change spans several parts that could each ship alone as a useful PR, spec now asks whether to file one issue per part, so each PR is reviewed against a smaller diff and fewer criteria. You can decline the split; a non-interactive run files one issue and records the recommended split. (#1662)
- **`/prflow:spec` drafts that loosen a check now name what happens to evidence they cannot read.** When a draft lets evidence exempt a case from a rule, or loosens, skips or demotes an outcome, its before→after mapping now covers each state in which that evidence cannot be read. Each state keeps its previous outcome unless the request names it; a new rule states each one's outcome. Implement then builds that behavior up front instead of review rejecting the PR once per uncovered input. (#1661)
- **`/prflow:spec` revisions delete attacked text before adding remedies.** When a review finding attacks draft text, a revision now deletes an unrequested criterion or moves derivable text to the investigation record instead of adding the finding's remedy, so review rounds stop growing the draft. (#1664)
- **`/prflow:spec` no longer copies both documentation-check reports into its Step 1 evidence file.** The file now holds a short record per lead (doc verdict and location, relevant files, and what it did not establish), so each spec run spends several thousand fewer output tokens and finishes Step 1 sooner. (#1659)
- **`Stricter than criterion` and `Disputed criterion` lines in a pull request description quote the criterion's text.** They no longer cite its number, so amending the issue can no longer point a line at the wrong criterion. A PR review counts a `Stricter` line only while its quoted text matches a current criterion; a line whose criterion was reworded or removed, or a numbered `Stricter` line written before this release, is ignored until a fix pass discloses again.

## September 30, 2026

- **The fix-delta gate now applies your review-and-fix extension.** The reviewer `/prflow:review-and-fix` runs over each fix iteration's changes now receives your `.prflow/skill-extensions/review-and-fix.md` rules as review policy, so the checks you wrote for it apply in the iteration that needs them. That reviewer sometimes runs without them — for example when the pull request changes the extension file, or when the file sits behind a symbolic link. (#1456)
- **The coverage, error-handling and code reviewers grade findings in the engine's severity words, with no scores.** The coverage reviewer (`pr-test-analyzer`) and the error-handling reviewer (`silent-failure-hunter`) label every finding Critical, Important or Suggestion, and the code reviewer (`code-reviewer`) labels every finding Critical or Important; none emits a numeric rating, a confidence score or a CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM band. A missing test for an edge case of working code is now a Suggestion, so at the default fix threshold `important` the fix loop reports it instead of writing the test, unless the convergence shadow's park calibration promotes it. A missing test is Important only when a changed function's main behavior is untested, and Critical only when its regression could lose or corrupt kept data, open a security hole or stop the whole system; a coverage gap the old scale rated highly for a user-facing error is no longer Critical by default. Code the coverage reviewer finds already wrong is reported as a defect graded by fail direction, so one that can lose data now reaches Critical, and a previous `test_gap` deferral no longer matches it until it is deferred again under its new kind. A code-reviewer finding that reached Critical only through a high confidence score is now Important, and a code-reviewer bug that can lose data, open a security hole or stop the system is now Critical. A recorded test-authoring waiver no longer lowers any review grade: review stops reading it, while the fix loop still does not re-impose waived ceremony on the surfaces a waiver names unless review grades that ceremony's finding Important or Critical. No verdict rule or threshold changes. (#1564)
- **`/prflow:spec` names the search behind every set of existing members it claims is complete, and re-runs it or marks it superseded when, for example, an answer or revision changes the design.** (#1438)
- **The review accepts a stricter-than-criterion fix disclosed in the PR description once a verifier confirms it against the code.** In a pull-request review, a `Stricter than criterion <N>: <case> — <why>` line starting a line of the PR description, with N a decided criterion's number, can now reach the checklist verifier for that criterion. When, among other conditions, the verifier confirms the code covers the case the line names and still meets every other case the criterion names, the criterion passes and a finding that only reports that departure moves to Informational — Deferred instead of driving a REJECT. A line the code does not bear out changes nothing, and a disclosure never clears a defect beyond the departure it names. The review's Run details list each line's outcome. (#1501)
- **`/prflow:spec` drafts now state a changed decision rule's full before→after effect.** A draft that changes a decision rule — for example a grade, route, verdict or guard — maps the rule's outcome per input class and mode with the old rule quoted, and reads every effect claim from that mapping; universal claims such as "nothing else moves" are now found by what they assert rather than by keyword. (#1579)
- **A review re-checks a failed checklist item it doubts before rejecting on it.** When the review's own reading of a file in the reviewed code contradicts the evidence behind a failed checklist item at or above your `verdict_severity_threshold`, the review sends that item back to a verifier once, with the doubt as a claim to check. The re-check's answer, a pass or a failure at its own severity, replaces the stored failure unless the source-view check rejects its evidence; an inconclusive or unusable re-check keeps the failure. Doubts resting on the pull request's text or an author's comment are not re-checked, and neither is an item settled by a text probe, an item whose cited file the review cannot read, or any item in a review whose verification results had to be written without the verdict helper. The report shows each doubt and its outcome only in `Run details`, instead of as a note under the failed item that changed nothing. Each re-check costs one more verification. (#1527)
- **The review-and-fix loop no longer runs its Loop Exit completion-evidence check under `/prflow:implement`.** There the implement run's own Phase 4.3 completion gate validates the final tree, so the loop builds no operand files, runs no validator, appends no `— completion evidence:` token to its verdict and records no reflection bullet for it — ending the run-after-run non-pass verdicts and forced retrospectives the check produced there. Standalone `/prflow:review-and-fix` and direct `/prflow:fix` runs keep the check unchanged. (#1529)
- **A re-review after a REJECT now always runs the full review.** It no longer re-checks only the named blockers of the earlier REJECT. The first re-review keeps the REJECT, whatever severity it grades the problem, when it finds still untrue a PR line that a finding of the earlier review rejected under the untrue-line rule; inside `/prflow:review-and-fix`, each later iteration that re-checks it keeps it too while that line stays untrue. A few review-side conditions stop this carry, for example a re-check item the review could not build correctly. (#1482)
- **A direct `/prflow:fix` pass reviews its own fixes before claiming completion.** A direct `/prflow:fix` pass that fixed at least one finding now has its own delta reviewed by one blinded subagent before it claims completion, using the review-and-fix loop's fix-delta checks. The completion claim adds a `fix-delta gate: <outcome>` line and reads "complete" only when the gate is clean, refixed, skipped (no fix applied) or pushed back. Verification Gate item 2 also treats a PR-body sentence the fix made false as a documented falsehood to fix.
- **`/prflow:spec` criteria over a multi-clause rule name every clause they touch.** `/prflow:spec` now makes a criterion or `Verified:` premise over a multi-clause rule name every clause, arm and ordering it touches, so a clause the draft never mentions no longer reaches review unaddressed.
- **`/prflow:spec` audit rounds route a missing dispatch pointer to a named failure.** `/prflow:spec` audit rounds now send a round whose instruction generator printed no dispatch pointer to a failure route that names that case, and the Step 3.6 boundary read gives `query-boundary`'s call form, so the orchestrator no longer passes it a `--draft-file` flag it rejects.
- **Rule pointers replace restatements only where the rule's home is loaded.** The review-and-fix loop now replaces a restated rule with a pointer to the rule's home only where that home is loaded wherever the pointer is read, and `/prflow:spec` keeps its universal-claim rule in one home with three load-scoped copies instead of restating its trigger in always-loaded files.
- **`/prflow:review` no longer skips an unreadable newer report in its prior-report re-check.** `/prflow:review`'s prior-report re-check no longer skips an unreadable comment newer than the report it would select: it records `prior-report: unavailable (comments-payload-malformed)`, capping the verdict at `APPROVE WITH CAVEAT`, instead of silently re-checking an older report.
- **`/prflow:review` waits for verifier verdicts in one call.** `/prflow:review` Phase 2 now ends each verifier fan-out message (the first wave and each refused-dispatch re-issue round) with one foreground `normalize-verdicts.py wait` call over the launched ids, so a local pass is no longer woken once per verifier hand-back. The new `wait` mode polls the verdicts directory until an `<id>-*.json` file exists for every id, the deadline passes, or the directory exists but cannot be listed; it prints `present`, `missing`, `waited_s` and `deadline_hit` and exits 0 (a usage error exits 2, and an unexpected exception prints the helper's internal-error object); ids still missing take the existing `verdict_file_absent` path unless the helper reports the directory not listable; that case and any other output fall back to collecting every dispatch as before.
- **A wrongly worded checklist item no longer rejects correct code.** `/prflow:review` no longer rejects a pull request over a checklist item worded wrongly while the code is right. A paraphrased item whose verifier answers `FAIL` with `inaccuracy_scope: none` and `property_proven: true` now gets one re-ask, and a re-ask that proves the property stores `PASS`. The checklist generator no longer paraphrases a source more narrowly than it reads, and requires untouched text to stay only when a criterion or named rule does.
- **A criterion dispute is now decided once and can reach the PR description.** A review-and-fix loop declines a finding over a disputed criterion once — for example, when the fix would contradict the criterion — then copies that decline forward and stops editing around the finding in later iterations. Before a criterion-conflict exit, for example a final REJECT whose every trigger is such a dispute, the loop now runs its blinded shadow pass; the verdict stays REJECT. Under `/prflow:implement`, each dispute can be written into the pull request description as a `Disputed criterion <N>:` line, so the maintainer can amend the criterion on the issue or accept it. (#1535)
- **`/prflow:review-and-fix` stops fixing findings the review deferred.** `/prflow:review-and-fix` no longer routes a finding the review demoted to `### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred` (an honored deferral, a confirmed stricter-than-criterion disclosure, or a disclosure foreclosure) to the fixer, the parked population or the shadow's promotion test when it can pair that report line to the finding. Pairing is exact: a line that matches no finding (a corroborated line whose merged instance list differs from each finding's included), matches several unrelated findings, or shares a finding with another line demotes nothing and is recorded as a `phase4-demotion unpaired:` note; so does an unreadable report. A demotion from a review the loop ran inline, without a dispatched engine agent, does not carry into later iterations.
- **A resumed `/prflow:implement` run can now reuse its earlier clean issue-claim audit and its committed Plan.** The Phase 1.6 reuse gate no longer counts the run's own `authorized-workpad-decision` items, and intake no longer files the run's own unfinished review work as a correction. A `Verified:` premise refuted only because the branch edited the cited file is recorded as a branch-changed note and nothing else, unless an earlier audit already flagged that bullet or the run cannot read its saved workpad. The Phase 2 resume gate no longer requires a Plan row for the run's own decisions or for verification, review and documentation obligations; it names each one it carries forward and still runs full discovery when it cannot classify an item. (#1528)
- **One workpad compaction now lasts a whole implement run.** `workpad.py compact` moves bullets
  down to a low watermark (`_COMPACT_LOW_WATER_BYTES` in `scripts/workpad.py`) instead of stopping
  just under the warning line, so the next few notes no longer trigger another compaction. The moved
  bullets are appended to the issue's newest overflow comment when it keeps its header lines and
  still has room, instead of a new comment on every call. The cloud-CI completion-evidence row is now stored compressed, and workpads
  written before this change stay readable. (#1547)
- **Review-and-fix now notes when a pull request edits its own review-and-fix extension.** On each shadow review pass, review-and-fix records a Reflections note when the pull request under review edits any of its review-and-fix extension files, when any of those files has local changes (untracked or ignored copies included), or when their provenance cannot be checked, because its calibration gates read that extension. A run that ends without a shadow pass records no note. The note blocks nothing, and a run whose provenance checks pass sees no change. (#1472)
- **`/prflow:spec` states one decided behavior per fork.** `/prflow:spec`'s no-options rule is now a short semantic rule instead of a word list with exemptions: an issue states one decided behavior per fork and leaves no alternative, open question or deferred choice outside `## 🚫 Blocked`. Wording the user approved, or wording the issue prescribes for the implementer to ship verbatim, is never reworded silently by any check (the check asks you instead), so a definition that uses "could" in its possibility sense keeps the meaning the user approved. Follow-up issues drafted by `/prflow:implement` and issues filed by the retrospective audit read the same rule. (#1569)
- **A re-review checks a `Disputed criterion <N>:` line against the criteria, so a point the criteria settle stops rejecting the PR.** `/prflow:implement` records a fix it declines because it would weaken or contradict criterion N as one `Disputed criterion <N>:` line at the end of the PR body; a direct `/prflow:fix` pass now does too. On the next review, the check that re-verifies an earlier failure reads the line with the issue's criteria and passes only when a criterion's words settle the point and the code shows it — for example, a criterion that excludes the arm the finding asks for. A finding that repeats only the earlier failure that check passed moves to Informational — Deferred. A line the criteria do not bear out changes nothing: the failure and the verdict stand. (#1441)
- **A resumed cloud implement run continues its review-and-fix loop instead of restarting at iteration 1.** Each fix-applying iteration now records the head it ends on (`iteration_head`), and a resume binds that record through base-merge commits added since, so a rate-limit or stall death costs only the interrupted iteration and the iteration cap holds. A resume that committed no new implementation work, with a clean tree, also skips the Phase 3.2 cleanup pass. A record written before this change carries no `iteration_head`, so a re-fix commit after the head it recorded ends its continuation; on the cloud tier, repositories with telemetry disabled keep the fresh start. (#1537)

## September 29, 2026

- **Untrue internal documentation no longer blocks a review.** `/prflow:review`: an untrue sentence in internal documentation that the review shows no tool or agent reads to decide behavior no longer blocks a review at a `critical` or `important` verdict threshold, while the report still lists it and the fix loop still corrects it when its stored severity meets the fix-severity threshold (#1425). Prose an agent loads as instructions (a skill or agent body, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, a prompt extension) now counts as behavior-affecting.
- **Review docs describe the internal-documentation cap.** `/prflow:review`'s published docs now state that an untrue sentence in internal documentation no tool or agent reads to decide behavior no longer blocks a review at a `critical` or `important` threshold, while the report still lists it and the fix loop still corrects it; `/prflow:fix` states that an untrue line in a README, published doc, release note or user-facing message always blocks (#1425).
- `/prflow:spec` now makes an issue account for the guards or guarantees it deletes or narrows and keeps a doc criterion from asking for a restatement of the conditions of the rule it describes, and `/prflow:implement`'s operand trace no longer counts agent recall across a subagent dispatch as a producing step — for example, a draft that deletes a guard names the mechanism still bounding it or accepts the loss, the approach menu offers deleting such a guard, the audit flags repairing one, and a doc criterion asks for a pointer or a one-line effect (#1516).
- **`/prflow:spec` Step 4 classifies its run-state files with a helper mode instead of reading `ls -lL` rows.** `scripts/cleanup-spec-run.sh --probe-run-state <slug> --root .` checks the run's two run-state files with bash file tests and prints one `path=<path> class=present|absent|unestablished` line for each, which the draft message shows; an empty or unsafe slug prints one `run_state=unestablished reason=unsafe-slug` line instead, and otherwise a missing or non-directory `--root` prints one `run_state=unestablished reason=no-root` line. The always-loaded skill text no longer carries the `ls` row-reading rules, and the classification no longer depends on which `ls` the host ships. (#1381)
- **`/prflow:spec` now widens an existing issue only from a non-empty body and reports the outcome accurately.** An update never sent is reported as not attempted, with the reason; a failed read-back as unverified rather than a failed write. (#1434)
- **A review now reports every instance of a defect class in the same pass.** Each reviewer checks the diff, and each file a finding names, for other instances of the class it found: sibling branches, mirrored or coupled sites, and restatements of the same claim. It groups one file's instances into one finding that names each with its line, and reports another file's instances as that file's own finding. A rejected pull request therefore gets the whole class in one round instead of one gap per round. The test-coverage reviewer lists every untested input shape, input combination, caller-supplied value and branch of a new or changed function that it rates 5 or higher, in one finding per function. A finding line can be longer, and a review can report fewer findings. No verdict rule or severity threshold changes: each instance keeps its own severity, and a grouped finding carries only the severity its most severe instance already had. (#1510)
- **Fixers and reviewers remove or point at a rule before adding to it.** Fixers, reviewers and implement's claim sweep now delete or point at a rule's home before adding — for example, a fixer deletes a failing claim before rewording it, and a reviewer's suggested fix leads with removal or reuse — docs passes point at a rule or describe its effect instead of restating it, and in `/prflow:fix` a fix that changes what a rule decides re-reads the issue's acceptance criteria; a fix stricter than a criterion is disclosed, for example as a `Stricter than criterion` line in the pull request description.
- **Review-and-fix now checks each working-tree copy of its extension before trusting the shadow review.** On runs that load the extension from the working tree (for example local, interactive and cloud implement runs), the shadow review's provenance check looked only at `.prflow/skill-extensions/review-and-fix.md`. It now also covers the legacy `.prflow/prompt-extensions/` file and the superseded `.devflow/` directory, so a pull request editing one of them is reported as not independently verified ("shadow agreement not verified"), the same as one that edits the canonical file. A symlinked extension file or extension directory now always reports the shadow as not independently verified, and so does a gitignored local copy of the extension. (#1513)
- **A review re-checks the defects the pull request's previous review reported.** A pull-request review, except one the blocker-recheck fast path settles, reads the newest PRFlow review progress comment on that pull request stamped with its posted verdict, other than its own, that GitHub Actions or an author your `allowed_bots` or `allowed_users` settings trust posted. A report voided as incomplete is passed over, and a `*` in `allowed_bots` trusts no bot beyond GitHub Actions and the ones it lists by name. Each failed checklist item and each finding in it, except a finding the report lists under Informational — Deferred, becomes a checklist item verified next to the freshly generated ones. One that still fails blocks the verdict like any other failed item; one that passes explains why the earlier evidence no longer holds. The report's `Run details` records which earlier report was used, or why none was (including how many untrusted reports were skipped). A review that could not establish the earlier report (for example, when the comments cannot be fetched or an author's permission cannot be checked), or whose re-check items did not all reach the checklist, is capped at APPROVE WITH CAVEAT, and so are the later passes of a review-and-fix loop after such a first pass. A later pass of a review-and-fix loop no longer drops an item the previous pass failed because the fix changed its file; it verifies the item again. Each re-checked defect costs one more verification. (#1512)

## September 28, 2026

- Spec loads contract guidance for Testing Strategy assertions and reuses quality-group rules during its draft check, reducing duplicated instructions. (#1378)
- **The default `claude_model` is now `claude-opus-5-5`.** New installs and re-scaffolds that lack a `claude_model` key get Claude Opus 5.5 instead of Claude Opus 5; an existing `claude_model` value is kept.
- **Unverifiable checklist items no longer reject a PR.** `/prflow:review` no longer rejects a pull request over a checklist item it could not verify. An INCONCLUSIVE item now gives APPROVE with notes at any `verdict_severity_threshold`, and the report lists it under a `### Unverified` heading for the human merger. The verdict is capped at APPROVE WITH CAVEAT when the checklist holds at least one item and every item is inconclusive, or when an item is inconclusive because verification itself fell short, such as a verifier that timed out. A checklist FAIL still rejects at or above the threshold. `/prflow:review-and-fix` no longer keeps a REJECT on an INCONCLUSIVE item, and on an APPROVE WITH CAVEAT verdict it still fixes findings and failed checklist items at or above `fix_severity_threshold`; a checklist item it left inconclusive that the final shadow review fails now counts as a new failure. The blocker-recheck fast path accepts a prior report with inconclusive items. (#1423)
- Share trigger-time configuration across command and implement workflows. A refreshed workflow now fails with an upgrade instruction when its installed config action lacks projection support or its projector script is missing or unreadable, including when the workflow is disabled in config. (#1397)
- **`/prflow:review-and-fix` reviews its own fixes before stopping.** `/prflow:review-and-fix` no longer stops early on a REJECT whose driver it fixed in the same iteration: when the iteration fixed a REJECT driver or any finding or failed checklist item at or above `fix_severity_threshold`, or its fix records cannot be confirmed, the loop runs one more iteration so the engine reviews the fixes, up to `max_iterations`. Any other REJECT still converges as before. `/prflow:implement`'s changed-contract sweep now also finds every reader of an output value whose inputs changed, such as a verdict, status, exit code or field value, and checks that each reader routes the new inputs. (#1439)
- **`/prflow:spec` now accounts for each universal-quantifier sentence it leaves unpinned.** Step 3.5's universal-quantifier sweep records how many quantifier sentences it pinned and removed, and each sentence it keeps unpinned with a locator and its reason, instead of a bare "no ungrounded universal quantifier" line. The universal-quantifier rule it applies now covers every universal quantifier asserted about the system under change outside `## 🚫 Blocked`, Implementation Notes included, so such a "never" or "always" sentence there must be pinned, scoped or removed unless it is mandated template boilerplate or rule text the change ships. (#1323)
- **`spec-context-eval.py` measures whole `/prflow:spec` runs.** `scripts/spec-context-eval.py` now measures a whole `/prflow:spec` run. A run starts at the first main-thread record labelled with the spec skill and ends at the end of its session file (in manifest mode, of its declared event span), so the records Claude Code writes without that label after a subagent hands back are counted too. `turn_count` counts API turns, and a response written as several records adds its output tokens once. In corpus and paired mode, a turn shared by a resumed or forked session file and the file it was copied from counts in at most one of them when they share a corpus (in paired mode, on the same side). Run records gain `cumulative_context`, the summary gains `median_turn_count` and `median_cumulative_context`, and the paired delta gains `mean_cumulative_context_per_run`. The skip channels a session folder's subagent transcripts, `.meta.json` and `custom-title.json` files and `tool-results/*.txt` files land in no longer make the paired context deltas read `unestablished`. The shared transcript reader, used by the cloud review job's evidence gate, now reads a JSONL record holding a raw U+2028, U+2029 or U+0085 as one record. (#1332)
- The shared marker readers now recognize CRLF marker lines, and the verdict-gap classifier no longer accepts trailing-text markers. COMMENTED reviews with a line-1 `<!-- prflow:review-verdict>` prefix now fail closed instead of being skipped during verdict selection. (#1398)
- **A pull request that edits the review-and-fix extension can complete after a clean review.** When a pull request edits `.prflow/skill-extensions/review-and-fix.md` and its shadow review runs as a `fanned-out` engine pass with no parent-issued reviewer dispatch, that edit no longer keeps the shadow agreement from being verified, so `/prflow:implement` no longer stops Blocked at finalization for that reason. An inline shadow of such a pull request is still reported as not independently verified. (#1468)
- `/prflow:implement` now rechecks the acceptance criteria when one of the sweeps it runs between writing and testing the code adds, removes or changes a path from a condition to an outcome that the plan does not describe, fixes or reverts a sweep change that makes false a criterion the issue's Desired Behavior supports, and can rewrite, or defer to a follow-up issue, criteria that recheck finds can no longer all be met. (#1457)
- **A cloud implement run that auto-resumes on its last allowed attempt is no longer reported as 💥 Failed.** When the agent job failed after the stall backstop had already posted the resume that reached `stall_backstop.max_resume_attempts`, the recovery job counted that resume, read the cap as exhausted, and marked the issue 💥 Failed with a "re-run manually" comment while the resumed run was starting. It now logs a warning and leaves the issue alone when its resume check reports a resume already posted for that run or reports that it could not read the issue's comments; otherwise it still marks the run 💥 Failed. (#1477)
- **A repeatedly skipped finding no longer stops `/prflow:review-and-fix`.** `/prflow:review-and-fix`: a finding skipped in two consecutive iterations no longer stops the loop. It still reports "Finding persists after pushback … Manual review needed.", now once per finding per run, and a finding the earlier iteration settled by disclosure still does not trigger it unless it drives the current REJECT. The loop then continues as it would without the repeat skip; for example, an iteration that ended in REJECT after fixing its driver now gets another review pass, up to the iteration cap. This holds for standalone runs as well as `/prflow:implement` runs.
- Acceptance-criterion verifiers now check the code's other branches under a criterion's condition before passing it (for example, an error path that silently allows the opposite outcome now fails the criterion). (#1458)
- **`/prflow:implement` restate re-dispatches no longer force `unmet`.** `/prflow:implement` Phase 3.4: a `restate-evidence` re-dispatch no longer tells the evidence verifier to record a measured value and report `unmet` whenever it differs from the stated terms. The prompt now only states that `satisfied` needs the two strings byte-equal, so the verifier's own rule decides when to copy the stated terms. The prompt no longer pushes a criterion met except for behavior a sibling criterion requires to `unmet`, so it can tick on restate.
- **Checklist claims state what must hold.** `/prflow:review`: the checklist generator now words every item's claim as what must hold — for an item about authored text, what that text asserts — and puts a suspected defect in the item's verify hint. Before, an item about authored text written as a suspected defect that the verifier disproved was stored as a FAIL that could not be normalized, so a proven-correct PR could be rejected with nothing to fix.
- **An implement run whose PR edits its own review-and-fix extension no longer stops Blocked at finalization.** When the fix loop's shadow returned every reviewer and raised nothing new, but its prompt attestation recorded only extension-provenance entries (the edited `.prflow/skill-extensions/review-and-fix.md`), the run recorded unverified shadow coverage with no admissible cause and stopped Blocked with the PR left draft. The run now records a `shadow-coverage` disposition with the new cause class `extension-provenance` and publishes; the workpad's disposition row and its Action-required reflection state that shadow agreement was not independently verified. `workpad.py` admits this cause only for the `shadow-coverage` gap and only when every always-on reviewer's roster row reads `dispatched` and no member reads `missing`. A run with any other prompt addendum still blocks. (#1484)
- Warn when a review progress comment cannot be marked failed, and stop the workflow’s stale-REJECT safety net from dismissing earlier change requests when the cloud review evidence gate fails. (#1293)
- **Aligned spec drafting guidance with its issue template.** The worked example now uses an already-chosen dependency and declares a documentation deliverable, and the creation step accurately points to the posting recipe. (#1380)
